# index.html.md

<!-- generated by epythet -->

# heed

**Embeddable, no-install, framework-agnostic end-user feedback** — a drop-in widget
that lets *any visitor* of your deployed web app report a bug or request a feature,
with useful context gathered automatically, routed to a pluggable backend (GitHub
Issues first). Works standalone; integrates cleanly with
[`enlace`](https://github.com/i2mint/enlace) as an optional add-on, and never needs an
enlace platform to run. It only reuses enlace’s stdlib-only rate-limit helpers, though
installing heed installs the `enlace` package with its own dependencies (uvicorn, cw).

> **Status: design phase.** The competitive landscape, the design rationale, and the
> roadmap live in [`misc/docs/`](). Work is tracked in GitHub
> [issues](https://github.com/i2mint/heed/issues); design decisions in GitHub
> [discussions](https://github.com/i2mint/heed/discussions).

## Why

Developer-side tools (browser extensions, Chrome DevTools MCP, Jam, …) only help
*you*. They can never serve an ordinary end user reporting a problem on your live
site, or asking for a feature. `heed` is the missing piece: a **public, zero-install**
capture-and-report widget plus a small self-hostable backend that *you* own and that
routes wherever you want.

## The shape (planned)

- **Widget** — one `<script>` tag injects a Shadow-DOM-isolated custom element; drops
  into React, plain HTML, or server-rendered pages alike. Captures a screenshot, page
  URL, and environment by default; console/network capture is *opt-in* (privacy).
- **Backend** — a mountable FastAPI router (run on its own, or mounted into `enlace`)
  that validates, stores attachments (via `dol`), and dispatches to a **pluggable
  sink**.
- **Sinks** (strategy pattern) — GitHub Issues / Discussions first; email, Slack, a
  built-in board, or a database later.
- **Agent hand-off** — an optional MCP server (`py2mcp`) so Claude Code can pull the
  feedback queue and act on reports.

## Design principles

- **Standalone first.** heed never needs an enlace platform: the router mounts in any
  FastAPI app. The one thing it takes from the `enlace` package is `enlace.ratelimit`
  (trusted-proxy client address + limiters, standard library only), so that security
  mechanism has one implementation and one test suite; mounting into enlace stays an
  optional `[enlace]` extra.
- **Privacy by default.** Heavy capture (console, network, session replay) is opt-in;
  PII masking is designed in, not bolted on.
- **Public endpoint = hostile input.** Rate limiting, origin checks, payload caps, and
  bot protection are first-class — the ingest endpoint is unauthenticated by nature.
- **Progressive disclosure.** One script tag works out of the box; everything is
  parametrizable via keyword-only options with smart defaults.

## Install

```bash
pip install heed                 # core (backend + models)
pip install "heed[github]"       # + GitHub sink
pip install "heed[enlace,mcp]"   # + enlace mount + MCP feedback queue
pip install "heed[redis]"        # + rate limits shared across workers
```

## Running the ingest endpoint safely

The `POST /report` endpoint is public, so it ships hardened: origin allow-list with CORS, streamed body/field/screenshot caps, strict input validation, per-IP and per-origin rate limits, a honeypot field, and an optional Turnstile/hCaptcha gate. Configure it in code or from `HEED_*` environment variables:

```python
from heed import HeedConfig, StoreSink, make_app

config = HeedConfig.from_env()   # e.g. HEED_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://myapp.example
app = make_app(StoreSink({}), config=config)
```

For production, set `allowed_origins`, `trusted_proxies` (behind a reverse proxy), `rate_limit_backend="redis"` with `redis_url` (several workers), and `bot_secret` to turn the bot gate on. Embedders also need a Content-Security-Policy that allows the widget: see [`misc/docs/embedding-security.md`]().

## One inbox for bugs, ideas and questions

The widget’s category picker sets `Report.category`; the sink decides what each category becomes:

```python
from heed import CategorySink, CategoryTreatment, GitHubIssuesSink, github_sink_from_token

issues = github_sink_from_token("myorg/myapp", token)   # bug -> labelled issue with full context;
                                                          # feature/question -> light issue (no env dump)
ideas = github_sink_from_token("myorg/ideas", token, public_label="board")
sink = CategorySink({"feature": ideas}, default=issues)  # or route a category to another sink
```

`GitHubIssuesSink(treatments={Category.feature: CategoryTreatment(("idea",), title_prefix="[idea] ")})` changes labels, title prefix and `detail` (“full” | “light”) per category. For a future public board, sinks that can list their items implement `public_items()`; the GitHub sink returns issues a maintainer labelled `public` as `PublicItem`s (title, category, status from labels or issue state, link, 👍 votes, dates, never the issue body or the reporter; the item’s link opens the issue itself, so keep the tracker public-safe), and for feature and question reports the server also drops the screenshot, console, network and browser details (`HeedConfig.light_categories`). `heed.roadmap(items)` / `heed.changelog(items)` are the two views over them.

## Embedding the widget

The backend serves the widget too, so a site adds one tag:

```html
<script async src="https://feedback.example/heed/widget/heed.js"></script>
```

Options (`data-*` or `heed.init({...})`), the `heed` API, the React wrapper, screenshots and their masking, pinning a build with SRI, events, theming and CSP notes: [`widget/README.md`]().

## Review pages: media with a comment thread under it

Publish a video, audio takes or images and get a link; whoever has it watches, reads the comments and adds their own (a name per comment, optionally pinned to a moment in the media), without an account:

```bash
heed review publish cut1.mp4 --title "Cut 1" --note-file notes.md   # prints the link
heed review publish cut2.mp4 --to <page-id>                          # a new cut, same link and thread
heed review comments <page-id> --json                                # read the feedback back
heed review publish cut2.mp4 --to <page-id> --password-file pw.txt --expires 7d   # gate it (pip install 'heed[gate]')
heed review revoke <page-id>                                          # end the link for everyone
```

A link sent to a client can carry a password, an expiry and a revoke (`heed.review_access`, on [caplinks](https://github.com/i2mint/caplinks); the `gate` extra): the page answers 401 until unlocked with the password (a cookie; wrong tries limited per client and per page), 410 once expired, 404 once revoked, and pages without any of it stay open as before. The link is a capability (128 random bits in the URL fragment); the thread endpoint is rate-limited, capped and honeypotted. Serve it with `make_review_app(rootdir, is_moderator=email_moderator([...]))`, or `heed review serve`. On an origin shared with other apps, a login is ambient authority (any script there acts as the owner), so require a typed-in secret instead: `is_moderator=token_moderator(secret, also=email_moderator([...]))` (`heed review serve --moderator-token-env VAR`); the review page’s *Moderate* button asks for it and keeps it in memory only. A dedicated origin (e.g. `review.<domain>`) is the stronger fix and is a deployment decision. The reusable part is `heed.threads` (a hardened comment thread per key, `make_thread_router`); `heed.review` is one consumer of it. Agents: the shipped skill `heed/data/skills/heed-review`. Rationale: [`misc/docs/adr/0001-review-pages-and-comment-threads-live-in-heed.md`]().

## Documents

- [`misc/docs/research-report.md`]() — the competitive
  landscape: what to reuse / steal / avoid, design patterns, and gotchas (deep
  research with adversarial verification).
- [`misc/docs/design.md`]() — architecture, the data model, the
  sink interface, and the spectrum of approaches with pros/cons.
- [`misc/docs/embedding-security.md`]() — hardening knobs for operators and CSP guidance for sites that embed the widget.

# heed.base

Domain model for heed — the single source of truth shared by widget and backend.

Everything that crosses the widget↔backend boundary, or moves between the ingest
layer and a sink, is one of the Pydantic models defined here. The widget POSTs a
[`ReportSubmission`](_autosummary/heed.base.html.md#heed.base.ReportSubmission) (what an untrusted client may assert); the backend enriches
it into a [`Report`](_autosummary/heed.base.html.md#heed.base.Report) (server-assigned id, timestamp, resolved identity, validated
origin, status) before handing it to a sink.

### heed.base.normalize_newlines(text)

Turn CRLF and lone CR into LF, so a line break counts as one character.

Browsers send every line break of a form field as CRLF; without this, a body at
the length limit would be refused for its line breaks.

```pycon
>>> normalize_newlines("a\r\nb\rc")
'a\nb\nc'
```

### heed.base.strip_control_chars(text)

Remove control characters (keeping tab/newline/CR) from untrusted text.

```pycon
>>> strip_control_chars("a\x00b\tc\u202ed")
'ab\tcd'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

Return the current UTC time (an injectable clock seam for tests).

* **Return type:**
  [`datetime`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime)


# _autosummary/heed.board.html.md

# heed.board

The read side of a feedback inbox: what a public board may show.

heed’s write path ends at a [`Sink`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.base.html.md#heed.sinks.base.Sink). A *board* (votes, a roadmap,
a changelog) is the read path over what the sinks accumulated, and it is a public
surface over untrusted, user-written text. This module fixes its shape before any UI
exists, so that the surface can be built on GitHub labels today and on a native store
later without touching the widget or the ingest layer:

- [`PublicItem`](_autosummary/heed.board.html.md#heed.board.PublicItem) – the **only** thing a board may expose: title, category, status,
  link, vote count, date. Never the body, identity, origin, environment or attachments.
- [`BoardSource`](_autosummary/heed.board.html.md#heed.board.BoardSource) – the protocol a sink implements to be listable
  (`BoardSource.public_items()`). [`BaseSink`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.base.html.md#heed.sinks.base.BaseSink) answers
  `[]`, so a sink that cannot list simply has an empty board.
- [`roadmap()`](_autosummary/heed.board.html.md#heed.board.roadmap) and [`changelog()`](_autosummary/heed.board.html.md#heed.board.changelog) – the two views the design names, as pure
  functions over items. Votes rank; status partitions.

Items reach a board only when an operator opts them in (for the GitHub sink, by a
`public` label), because an unmoderated visitor title on a public page is an abuse
vector (`misc/docs/embedding-security.md`).

```pycon
>>> from heed.base import Category, Status
>>> items = [
...     PublicItem(ref="1", title="Dark mode", category=Category.feature,
...                status=Status.planned, votes=5),
...     PublicItem(ref="2", title="Export CSV", category=Category.feature,
...                status=Status.completed, votes=9),
...     PublicItem(ref="3", title="Offline", category=Category.feature,
...                status=Status.triaged, votes=1),
... ]
>>> [i.title for i in roadmap(items)]
['Dark mode', 'Offline']
>>> [i.title for i in changelog(items)]
['Export CSV']
```

|---------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`CHANGELOG_STATUSES`](_autosummary/heed.board.html.md#heed.board.CHANGELOG_STATUSES) | Statuses that mean "shipped" (shown in a changelog).                         |

### Functions

|---------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|

# _autosummary/heed.config.html.md

# heed.config

Configuration for the heed backend (smart defaults; keyword-only).

Every knob has a safe default, so `HeedConfig()` works out of the box for a
single-worker deployment. [`HeedConfig.from_env()`](_autosummary/heed.config.html.md#heed.config.HeedConfig.from_env) reads the same knobs from
`HEED_*` environment variables, which is where secrets (the bot-gate key) and
infrastructure (the Redis URL) belong.

### Classes

| [`HeedConfig`](_autosummary/heed.config.html.md#heed.config.HeedConfig)(\*[, allowed_origins, ...])   | Knobs for the ingest endpoint.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|

### *class* heed.config.HeedConfig(\*, allowed_origins=None, handle_cors=True, cors_allow_credentials=False, cors_max_age_seconds=600, max_body_bytes=6000000, max_screenshot_bytes=5000000, screenshot_sanitizer='auto', max_screenshot_pixels=8500000, max_concurrent_reencodes=2, reencode_busy_wait_seconds=2.0, reencode_retry_after_seconds=5, max_field_bytes=100000, max_form_fields=16, rate_limit_per_minute=30, origin_rate_limit_per_minute=600, rate_limit_window_seconds=60.0, rate_limit_backend='memory', redis_url=None, redis_socket_timeout_seconds=0.5, rate_limit_max_keys=100000, trusted_proxies=list(), ipv6_rate_limit_prefix=64, limiter_threads=16, bot_verify_threads=8, reencode_threads=4, delivery_threads=8, bot_gate=None, bot_secret=None, bot_expected_hostnames=None, bot_token_field='bot_token', honeypot_field='hp_website', attachment_signing_key=None, attachment_url_ttl_seconds=None, attachment_previous_keys=list(), attachment_hosts=None, attachment_cache_control=None, accept_console=False, accept_network=False, mask_page_url=True, light_categories=<factory>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Knobs for the ingest endpoint. All optional with sensible defaults.

#### *property* bot_gate_enabled *: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*

True when a bot-gate secret is configured.

#### *classmethod* from_env(environ=None, \*\*overrides)

Build a config from `HEED_<FIELD>` variables, then apply `overrides`.

Lists are comma-separated; booleans accept 1/true/yes/on; `none` unsets an
optional knob (e.g. `HEED_ORIGIN_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=none`).

```pycon
>>> cfg = HeedConfig.from_env(
...     {"HEED_ALLOWED_ORIGINS": "https://a.example, https://b.example",
...      "HEED_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE": "10"}
... )
>>> cfg.allowed_origins, cfg.rate_limit_per_minute
(['https://a.example', 'https://b.example'], 10)
```

# _autosummary/heed.dedup.html.md

# heed.dedup

Duplicate detection in two stages: cheap retrieval, then confirmation (#8).

1. **Retrieval** ranks the stored reports by word overlap with the incoming one
   (title counted twice, body once; Jaccard over folded words) and keeps the
   `k` best above `min_score`. No model, no index: fine for a feedback queue.
2. **Confirmation** (optional) asks an injected `confirm(new, candidate) -> float`
   judge, e.g. an LLM or an embedding similarity, and keeps those it scores at
   `confirm_threshold` or more.

The result is a list of [`DupCandidate`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.base.html.md#heed.sinks.base.DupCandidate); nothing is merged.
[`mark_duplicate()`](_autosummary/heed.dedup.html.md#heed.dedup.mark_duplicate) records a decision on the stored report (`status` becomes
`duplicate` and `extra["duplicate_of"]` names the original), so a human or an
agent applies it explicitly.

```pycon
>>> from heed.base import Identity, Report
>>> me = Identity(anon_id="a")
>>> old = Report(id="r1", title="Save button crashes the app", identity=me)
>>> new = Report(id="r2", title="App crashes when I press save", identity=me)
>>> [c.external_ref for c in find_duplicates(new, [old])]
['r1']
```

### Module Attributes

| [`Confirm`](_autosummary/heed.dedup.html.md#heed.dedup.Confirm)   | the confirming judge.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------|

### Functions

| [`find_duplicates`](_autosummary/heed.dedup.html.md#heed.dedup.find_duplicates)(report, candidates, \*[, k, ...])   | Likely duplicates of `report` among `candidates`, best first.               |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`mark_duplicate`](_autosummary/heed.dedup.html.md#heed.dedup.mark_duplicate)(store, report_id, \*, of)            | Record that stored report `report_id` duplicates `of` (both must exist).    |
| [`stored_reports`](_autosummary/heed.dedup.html.md#heed.dedup.stored_reports)(store)                               | The reports in a StoreSink store (entries that do not parse are skipped).   |
| [`word_similarity`](_autosummary/heed.dedup.html.md#heed.dedup.word_similarity)(a, b)                               | Jaccard similarity of the reports' folded words (title words weigh double). |

### heed.dedup.Confirm

the confirming judge.

* **Type:**
  `(incoming, candidate) -> similarity in [0, 1]`

alias of [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Report`](_autosummary/heed.base.html.md#heed.base.Report), [`Report`](_autosummary/heed.base.html.md#heed.base.Report)], [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]

### heed.dedup.find_duplicates(report, candidates, , k=5, min_score=0.25, confirm=None, confirm_threshold=0.5)

Likely duplicates of `report` among `candidates`, best first.

Reports already marked duplicate, and `report` itself, are skipped. With
`confirm`, each retrieved candidate is re-scored by it and kept only at
`confirm_threshold` or more; a judge that raises drops that candidate.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`DupCandidate`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.base.html.md#heed.sinks.base.DupCandidate)]

### heed.dedup.mark_duplicate(store, report_id, , of)

Record that stored report `report_id` duplicates `of` (both must exist).

* **Return type:**
  [`Report`](_autosummary/heed.base.html.md#heed.base.Report)

### heed.dedup.stored_reports(store)

The reports in a StoreSink store (entries that do not parse are skipped).

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`Report`](_autosummary/heed.base.html.md#heed.base.Report)]

### heed.dedup.word_similarity(a, b)

Jaccard similarity of the reports’ folded words (title words weigh double).

```pycon
>>> from heed.base import Identity, Report
>>> me = Identity(anon_id="a")
>>> word_similarity(Report(title="Dark mode", identity=me),
...                 Report(title="dark  MODE please", identity=me))
0.6667
```

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)


# _autosummary/heed.html.md

# heed

heed — embeddable, no-install, framework-agnostic end-user feedback.

`heed` lets any visitor of a deployed web app report a bug or request a feature, with
useful context gathered automatically, routed to a pluggable backend (GitHub Issues
first). It works standalone and integrates with `enlace` as an optional add-on; the
only part of enlace it uses is the stdlib-only `enlace.ratelimit` (trusted-proxy
client address and limiters), shared so the mechanism is implemented once.

Phase 1 ships the backend core and the embeddable widget (`widget/`, served by
[`make_widget_router()`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.make_widget_router)). The competitive
landscape and design rationale live in `misc/docs/`.

Public API (Phase 1):
: Models    Report, ReportSubmission, Identity, Environment, Category, Status,
  : Attachment, LogEntry, NetEntry
  <br/>
  Sinks     Sink, BaseSink, SinkResult, StoreSink, GitHubIssuesSink,
  : github_sink_from_token
  <br/>
  Backend   process_submission, make_router, make_app, HeedConfig
  Hardening RateLimiter, InMemoryRateLimiter, RedisRateLimiter, make_rate_limiter,
  <br/>
  > BotVerifier, SiteverifyBotVerifier, make_bot_verifier,
  > make_image_sanitizer, strip_image, reencode_image, attachment_headers
  > (see misc/docs/embedding-security.md)
  <br/>
  Privacy   redact_text, redact_url (masking of opt-in console/network capture)
  Routing   sinks_by_origin, Verdict, accept_all, hold_all,
  <br/>
  > make_heuristic_moderator, chain_moderators, release_held,
  > recover_claimed, discard_held
  <br/>
  Storage   make_report_store, make_holding_store, make_attachment_store
  Serving   make_attachment_router, make_attachment_app, AttachmentSigner,
  <br/>
  > screenshot_url_resolver (a separate origin for screenshots, #19)
  <br/>
  Widget    make_widget_router (serves the built embeddable widget),
  : widget_contract (what the widget sends; SSOT for widget/)
  <br/>
  Threads   Comment, CommentSubmission, add_comment, list_comments,
  : delete_comment, email_moderator, token_moderator,
    make_thread_router (a public, persistent comment thread per key)
  <br/>
  Review    ReviewPage, publish_review, review_url, make_review_app (media + a
  : thread under it, behind a capability link; CLI `heed review`)
  <br/>
  Triage    triage, Triage, Severity (a proposal per report: injected LLM,
  : fenced and whitelisted, or keyword rules without one);
    find_duplicates, mark_duplicate (retrieval + optional confirmation;
    marking is explicit, never a silent merge); FeedbackQueue (list / get /
    triage / dedup / create / close; `heed.mcp` serves it over MCP)

### Example

```pycon
>>> from heed import StoreSink, ReportSubmission, process_submission
>>> store = {}
>>> report, result = process_submission(
...     ReportSubmission(title="Login button does nothing"), StoreSink(store)
... )
>>> result.ok and report.id in store
True
```

### *class* heed.AttachmentSigner(key, \*, previous_keys=(), ttl_seconds=None, clock=<built-in function time>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Mint and check signed attachment URLs (HMAC-SHA256 over the ref and expiry).

`ttl_seconds=None` (the default) signs URLs that never expire: a GitHub issue
keeps showing its screenshot, and access is revoked by deleting the attachment or
rotating the key. A ttl makes URLs expire, which suits links handed to people rather
than embedded in issues. `previous_keys` still verify (never sign), for rotation.

```pycon
>>> s = AttachmentSigner("k" * 32, ttl_seconds=60, clock=lambda: 1000)
>>> q = s.sign("ab.png")
>>> q["exp"], s.verify("ab.png", **q), s.verify("other.png", **q)
('1060', True, False)
>>> later = AttachmentSigner("k" * 32, ttl_seconds=60, clock=lambda: 2000)
>>> later.verify("ab.png", **q)
False
```

#### *classmethod* from_config(config, \*\*kwargs)

The signer `config` describes, or None if it has no signing key.

* **Return type:**
  [`AttachmentSigner`](_autosummary/heed.serving.html.md#heed.serving.AttachmentSigner) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### sign(ref)

The query parameters authorising `ref`: `sig`, and `exp` with a ttl.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### url(base_url, ref)

`{base_url}/{ref}?...`: the signed URL of `ref` under `base_url`.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### *classmethod* from_env(environ=None, \*\*overrides)

Build a config from `HEED_<FIELD>` variables, then apply `overrides`.

Lists are comma-separated; booleans accept 1/true/yes/on; `none` unsets an
optional knob (e.g. `HEED_ORIGIN_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=none`).

```pycon
>>> cfg = HeedConfig.from_env(
...     {"HEED_ALLOWED_ORIGINS": "https://a.example, https://b.example",
...      "HEED_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE": "10"}
... )
>>> cfg.allowed_origins, cfg.rate_limit_per_minute
(['https://a.example', 'https://b.example'], 10)
```

  [`HeedConfig`](_autosummary/heed.config.html.md#heed.config.HeedConfig)

### *class* heed.InMemoryRateLimiter(\*, max_per_window=30, window_seconds=60.0, max_keys=100000, clock=<built-in function monotonic>)

Bases: `_WindowKnobs`, `SlidingWindowLimiter`

Sliding-window, in-memory limiter. Per process — NOT shared across workers.

Fine for a single-worker deployment; with several workers each one counts alone,
so the effective limit is multiplied. Use [`RedisRateLimiter`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.RedisRateLimiter) there. The
number of tracked keys is bounded (`max_keys`, least-recently-seen evicted) so a
flood of distinct keys cannot exhaust memory.

### *class* heed.RedisRateLimiter(client, \*, max_per_window=30, window_seconds=60.0, namespace='heed:rl', fallback=None, max_keys=100000, clock=<built-in function time>)

Bases: `_WindowKnobs`, `RedisLimiter`

Fixed-window limiter in Redis — one count shared by every worker and host.

`client` is any redis-py compatible client (injected; tests use a fake). When
Redis errors, the request is decided by `fallback` (a per-process in-memory
limiter by default), so an outage degrades protection instead of either dropping
all feedback or removing the limit. `from_url()` builds the client from a
`redis://` URL (needs the `[redis]` extra).

After a Redis error the fallback alone decides for `retry_seconds` (5 s by
default) before Redis is tried again, so a hung Redis costs one socket timeout
per interval, not one per request; one warning per outage is logged, on the
`enlace.ratelimit` logger. An `allow`-only `fallback` is wrapped to answer
`acquire` too, so `.fallback` is then that wrapper (its `.limiter` is
yours). Counters are named `{namespace}:{window}:{key}:{window number}`.

#### install_hint *= "pip install 'heed[redis]'"*

Shown when the optional `redis` client is not installed.

### heed.attachment_headers(media_type, , filename=None, cross_origin=False)

Headers for serving a stored screenshot (issue #15). Use them on every response
that returns attachment bytes, ideally from an origin separate from the app’s.

Only the image types heed accepts are served as themselves; anything else is sent as
an opaque download. Embedding is limited to the same site
(`Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-site`) unless `cross_origin=True`, which a
screenshot embedded elsewhere (e.g. in a GitHub issue) needs.

```pycon
>>> h = attachment_headers("image/png", filename="r1.png")
>>> h["Content-Type"], h["X-Content-Type-Options"], h["Content-Disposition"]
('image/png', 'nosniff', 'inline; filename="r1.png"')
>>> attachment_headers("text/html")["Content-Type"]
'application/octet-stream'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### heed.discard_held(report_id, , holding_store, attachment_store=None)

Delete a held report for good, with its attachments (e.g. a screenshot).

The report leaves holding first, so a release that took it meanwhile wins and this
raises `KeyError` before touching its attachments; a crash between the two steps
leaves an orphaned screenshot, never a report pointing at a deleted one. Raises
`KeyError` when `report_id` is not held. A report whose text no longer parses is
still deleted, but its attachments cannot be named and are left. Run it serialised
with [`release_held()`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.release_held) for the same report.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### heed.make_attachment_router(attachment_store, , config=None, signer=None, allow_unsigned=False, allowed_hosts=None, cross_origin=False, cache_control=None, max_bytes=None, path='/attachments', ref_pattern=re.compile('[0-9a-f]{32}\\\\.(?:png|jpg|webp)'))

A router serving `GET {path}/{ref}` from `attachment_store`, read-only.

Every response that returns bytes carries `attachment_headers`; the bytes are
re-sniffed, and anything that is not the image its extension names is sent as an
opaque download. A missing, malformed, unsigned or expired ref is the same bare 404,
so the route is no oracle for which reports exist; a wrong `Host` is a 421 (a
deployment error worth seeing). Behind a reverse proxy, the `Host` checked is the
one the proxy forwards: keep it the browser’s (Caddy and nginx can).

* **Parameters:**
  * **attachment_store** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)]) – Where `process_submission` put the screenshots.
  * **config** ([`HeedConfig`](_autosummary/heed.config.html.md#heed.config.HeedConfig) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Defaults for `signer` (`attachment_signing_key`,
    `attachment_url_ttl_seconds`) and `allowed_hosts`
    (`attachment_hosts`).
  * **signer** ([`AttachmentSigner`](_autosummary/heed.serving.html.md#heed.serving.AttachmentSigner) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Required unless `allow_unsigned`: report ids are not secret.
  * **allow_unsigned** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Serve any ref without a signature (a ref is then the
    capability). Only for stores whose every screenshot may be public.
  * **allowed_hosts** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Hostnames this route answers on: the dedicated attachment origin.
    Required (here or as `config.attachment_hosts`): `ANY_HOST` says any
    host is fine, which is only right when the route has no origin of its own.
  * **cross_origin** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin`, which an image
    embedded in a GitHub issue needs (GitHub’s camo proxy fetches it).
  * **cache_control** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Replaces the `Cache-Control` of a served image (default
    `private, no-store`), e.g. `public, max-age=300` if GitHub’s camo proxy
    should cache signed, cross-origin images. Defaults to
    `config.attachment_cache_control`.
  * **max_bytes** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Stored values larger than this are not served (a bare 404 and a
    warning). Defaults to `config.max_screenshot_bytes`. It does not stop a
    store from reading the value into memory; it keeps serving from relying on
    the ingest cap alone.
  * **ref_pattern** ([`Pattern`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/re.html#re.Pattern)) – Refs to serve (full match); the default is what heed writes.
* **Return type:**
  `APIRouter`

### heed.make_attachment_store(rootdir=None, \*, delete_func=<built-in function remove>, follow_symlinks=False)

A bytes store for attachments. In-memory unless `rootdir` is given.

Deletion is permanent by default, for the reason given in `make_report_store`.
Reading a key whose file is a symlink leading outside `rootdir` raises
`KeyError`, so a misconfigured root cannot make the attachment route serve other
files; `follow_symlinks=True` opts out.

```pycon
>>> make_attachment_store()
{}
```

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)

### heed.make_bot_verifier(provider, secret, \*\*kwargs)

Return a verifier, or `None` (gate off) when no secret is configured.

`provider` defaults to `"turnstile"` when a secret is given.

* **Return type:**
  [`BotVerifier`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.BotVerifier) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### heed.make_heuristic_moderator(, max_links=3, blocked_terms=(), on_blocked_term=Verdict.hold)

Hold reports with more than `max_links` links or any of `blocked_terms`.

Cheap, dependency-free spam signals. Holding (not rejecting) is the default so a
false positive costs a human click, not a lost report.

```pycon
>>> mod = make_heuristic_moderator(max_links=1, blocked_terms=["casino"])
>>> from heed.base import Identity
>>> def r(body): return Report(title="t", body=body, identity=Identity(anon_id="a"))
>>> [mod(r(b)).value for b in ["ok", "http://a http://b", "best CASINO"]]
['accept', 'hold', 'hold']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Report`](_autosummary/heed.base.html.md#heed.base.Report)], [`Verdict`](_autosummary/heed.routing.html.md#heed.routing.Verdict)]

### heed.make_holding_store(rootdir=None, \*, delete_func=<built-in function remove>)

A report store for held reports, with a dedicated claims store beside it.

`release_held` and `recover_claimed` find the claims store on the holding store
(`heed_claims`), so a release lists only the reports being released right now,
not every held report (issue #21), and nothing listing holding (a moderation view,
`StoreSink.find_duplicates`) ever sees a claim. With `rootdir`, claims live in a
sibling directory, `<rootdir>.claims` (a subdirectory would show up in the
holding store’s recursive listing).

```pycon
>>> held = make_holding_store()
>>> held["r1"] = "{}"
>>> list(held), dict(held.heed_claims)
(['r1'], {})
```

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)

### heed.make_image_sanitizer(name='auto', , max_pixels=8500000, max_concurrent=2, busy_wait_seconds=2.0)

Build a sanitizer from the `image_sanitizers` registry by name.

Fails at construction (not on the first upload) when the name is unknown or its
dependency is missing.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)]

### heed.make_rate_limiter(backend='memory', , max_per_window, window_seconds=60.0, namespace='ip', redis_url=None, max_keys=100000, redis_socket_timeout=0.5)

Build a limiter from the `rate_limiter_backends` registry by name.

* **Return type:**
  [`RateLimiter`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.RateLimiter)

### heed.make_report_store(rootdir=None, \*, delete_func=<built-in function remove>)

A text store for report JSON. In-memory unless `rootdir` is given.

Deleting a key removes the file for good (`os.remove`). dol’s own default moves it
to the OS trash, which would keep a copy of every deleted, claimed or released
report – and reports can carry personal data. Pass `delete_func` to opt back in.

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)

### heed.make_review_app(rootdir=None, \*, is_moderator=<function no_moderator>, trusted_proxies=(), rate_limiter=None, rate_limit_per_minute=10, max_comments_per_thread=500, serve_shell=True, gate=None)

The review API (and, with `serve_shell`, the page at `/`).

Routes: `GET /pages/{id}`, `GET /pages/{id}/media/{name}` (byte ranges;
`?download=1` serves it as an attachment, so a phone saves the file),
`GET|POST /threads/{id}`, `DELETE /threads/{id}/{comment}` (moderators),
`GET /ui/review.{js,css}`. There is deliberately no HTTP listing of pages:
it would hand every capability to any script running as the owner (the CLI’s
`ls` lists them).

A page given a password, an expiry or a revoke ([`publish_review()`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.publish_review),
`heed review revoke`) is gated by `gate` (a `ReviewGate`, built over
`rootdir` with `trusted_proxies` by default): 401 until `POST
/pages/{id}/unlock` `{"password": ...}` sets a cookie, 410 once expired, 404
once revoked. Pages with no such record are open, as ever.

* **Return type:**
  `FastAPI`

### heed.make_router(sink, \*, config=None, attachment_store=None, rate_limiter=None, origin_rate_limiter=None, bot_verifier=None, user_dependency=None, resolve_sink=None, moderator=None, holding_sink=None, image_sanitizer=None, redactor=<function redact_text>)

Build a FastAPI APIRouter exposing `POST /report` (and its CORS preflight).

Run standalone via [`make_app()`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.make_app), or `include_router` it into an enlace app.
Provide `user_dependency` (a FastAPI dependency returning a user id or None) to
bind identity when an auth layer like enlace_auth is present.

Hardening defaults come from `config`; any piece can be injected instead:
`rate_limiter` (per client IP), `origin_rate_limiter` (per Origin) and
`bot_verifier` (by default built from `config.bot_secret`, i.e. off until a
secret is configured) and `image_sanitizer` (by default from
`config.screenshot_sanitizer`: re-encode with Pillow, else a pure-Python strip).
Opt-in console/network capture (`config.accept_console`/`accept_network`) is
masked by `redactor` before any sink sees it; a field the config does not accept
is never parsed.

Routing is decided server-side, never by the browser: `resolve_sink` maps the
validated origin to that site’s sink (`sink` is then the fallback and may be
None; an origin resolving to no sink gets 403). `moderator` may hold reports in
`holding_sink` (required with a moderator) or reject them; see `routing.py`.

* **Return type:**
  `APIRouter`

### heed.make_thread_router(threads=None, \*, thread_exists=<function valid_id>, is_moderator=<function no_moderator>, rate_limiter=None, rate_limit_per_minute=10, thread_rate_limiter=None, thread_rate_limit_per_hour=120, max_comments_per_thread=500, trusted_proxies=(), honeypot_field='website', on_comment=None, thread_gate=None)

The HTTP surface of comment threads (`threads`: thread id -> its store).

`GET /threads/{thread}` lists, `POST /threads/{thread}` adds (a JSON body:
`author`, `body`, optional `at_ms` and `media`),
`DELETE /threads/{thread}/{id}` deletes when `is_moderator(request)` and the
request carries the `X-Heed-Moderate` header. A thread for which
`thread_exists` is false answers 404 to everything, which is how a host makes
threads capabilities; `thread_gate(request, thread)` is called on every request
to an existing thread and raises `HTTPException` to refuse it (a password, say).
A filled `honeypot_field` is accepted silently and
stored nowhere. Behind a reverse proxy, set `trusted_proxies` or every visitor
shares the proxy’s rate-limit bucket.

```pycon
>>> from fastapi import FastAPI
>>> from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
>>> app = FastAPI(); app.include_router(make_thread_router())
>>> client = TestClient(app)
>>> client.post("/threads/t1", json={"author": "Thor", "body": "hi"}).status_code
201
>>> [c["body"] for c in client.get("/threads/t1").json()["comments"]]
['hi']
```

* **Return type:**
  `APIRouter`

### heed.make_widget_router(, asset_dir=None)

A router serving the built widget at `GET /widget/{name}`.

Include it beside [`heed.make_router()`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.make_router) (`make_app` does) so the widget is
served from the same host that receives its reports. `asset_dir` defaults to the
files shipped in the package; point it elsewhere to serve another build.

* **Return type:**
  `APIRouter`

### heed.mark_duplicate(store, report_id, , of)

Record that stored report `report_id` duplicates `of` (both must exist).

* **Return type:**
  [`Report`](_autosummary/heed.base.html.md#heed.base.Report)

### heed.new_report_id()

Return a fresh opaque report id (uuid4 hex).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### heed.process_submission(submission, sink, \*, origin='', user=None, screenshot=None, screenshot_media_type='image/png', attachment_store=None, config=None, id_gen=<function new_report_id>, clock=<function utcnow>, moderator=<function accept_all>, holding_sink=None, redactor=<function redact_text>)

Enrich `submission` into a Report, store any screenshot, and route to `sink`.

Returns the (report, sink-result) pair. The server owns id/created_at/identity/
origin/status — never the client. Opt-in capture (console/network) is dropped
unless enabled in `config`, and what is kept is passed through `redactor`
(personal data and secrets masked, see `redact.py`) whatever the widget did.
`moderator` decides first: `hold` sends the report
(status `held`) to `holding_sink` instead, `reject` drops it (status
`declined`).

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`Report`](_autosummary/heed.base.html.md#heed.base.Report), [`SinkResult`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.base.html.md#heed.sinks.base.SinkResult)]

### heed.publish_review(media, , title=None, note=None, rootdir=None, to=None, password=None, expires=None)

Publish `media` as a new review page (or add it to page `to`).

`password` and `expires` (`"7d"`, `"2026-11-01"`, `"never"`) gate the
page ([`heed.review_access`](_autosummary/heed.review_access.html.md#module-heed.review_access), needs `heed[gate]`); on an existing page they
change only what is given. Neither: the page is open to whoever has the link.

The files are copied into the data root. Adding to an existing page keeps its
link and its thread, so a new cut can go where the old one’s comments are; a file
with the name of one already on the page replaces it.

* **Return type:**
  [`ReviewPage`](_autosummary/heed.review.html.md#heed.review.ReviewPage)

### heed.recover_claimed(\*, holding_store, claimed_store=None, stale_after=None, clock=<built-in function time>)

Return every claimed report to holding, and the ids returned.

A claim outlives its [`release_held()`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.release_held) only if the process died mid-release
(the sink may or may not have accepted the report, so a recovered report may be
sent twice – never zero times). Pass the same `claimed_store` as to
[`release_held()`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.release_held).

An in-flight release’s claim looks the same as a stranded one. With one process,
call this when no release is running (e.g. at startup) and leave `stale_after`
unset: every claim is recovered. With several workers, one worker’s startup can
overlap another’s release, so pass `stale_after` (seconds; longer than any sink
call can take plus the clock skew between workers, e.g. `600`): only claims older
than that are recovered (and claims stamped further ahead than that, by a clock
running fast). Claims made before claim keys carried a time count as stale. A
release whose claim is recovered anyway puts the report back in holding and fails.
Beside a dedicated claims store, `claimed--` claims an older heed left in holding
are recovered too (which lists holding once).

Only a valid report (whose own id matches its claim key) is ever written to
holding, and a valid holding copy is never replaced: a claim whose report is
intact in holding is just dropped (even a torn one), and one whose holding copy
is torn or missing restores it. Otherwise a claim that is not a valid report is
left in place, and not returned.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### heed.redact_text(text)

Replace personal data and secrets in `text` by placeholders.

```pycon
>>> redact_text("Authorization: Bearer abc.def.ghi")
'Authorization: [redacted]'
>>> redact_text("paid with 4111 1111 1111 1111, order 1234567890123")
'paid with [card], order 1234567890123'
>>> redact_text('{"password": "hunter2", "user": "ana"}')
'{"password": "[redacted]", "user": "ana"}'
```

URLs in the text are masked like request URLs ([`redact_url()`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.redact_url)) first:

```pycon
>>> redact_text("callback https://app.example/cb?code=4/0AbC&state=x failed")
'callback https://app.example/cb?code=[redacted]&state=[redacted] failed'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### heed.redact_url(url, \*, redactor=<function redact_text>)

`url` without credentials, fragment or query values (keys are kept).

Path segments that look like ids (all digits, or 12+ characters with a digit) or
handles (`@name`) are replaced, path parameters dropped, and the rest of each
segment redacted as text.

```pycon
>>> redact_url("/api/users/ana@example.com?q=1")
'/api/users/[email]?q=[redacted]'
>>> redact_url("https://app.example/reset/9f8e7d6c5b4a3f2e;jsessionid=X/42")
'https://app.example/reset/[id]/[id]'
>>> redact_url("https://app.example/r/AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOpQr%2Fx/eyJhbGci.eyJzdWIi.sigpart")
'https://app.example/r/[id]/[id]'
>>> redact_url("mailto:ana@example.com")
'mailto:[redacted]'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### heed.reencode_image(data, media_type, , max_pixels=8500000)

Strip `data`, then decode it and save its first frame afresh, same format.

Images over `max_pixels` are refused before any pixel is decoded (a small file can
declare a huge canvas). Nothing but pixels (and PNG palette transparency) is carried
over: no comment, EXIF, ICC profile or other metadata. Raises `ValueError` on a
malformed, oversized or too costly image.

* **Return type:**
  [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)

### heed.release_held(report_id, \*, holding_store, sink=None, resolve_sink=None, claimed_store=None, clock=<built-in function time>)

Release a held report: route it on and remove it from holding.

`holding_store` is the store behind the holding sink (a `StoreSink`’s
`.store`). The destination is `sink`, or — for a multi-site backend — the sink
`resolve_sink` gives for the report’s own origin (pass exactly one).

The report is claimed before submitting, so a second release while the first is in
flight finds nothing to send. Claiming *moves* it: it is written under a claim key
of its own (`<id>--<time>-<token>`) in the claims store and only then deleted
from holding. The claims store is `claimed_store` if given, else the one a
`make_holding_store` store carries, else (legacy) `holding_store` itself under a
`claimed--` prefix – which makes every release list the whole holding store.
If the sink fails the report is put back in holding; a release only ever
deletes its own claim, and only once the sink has accepted the report or it is
back in holding. So a crash at any point leaves the report in holding, in the
claims, or in both – never lost – and [`recover_claimed()`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.recover_claimed) returns stranded
claims to holding. A report with a claim is not released again until then.

Not safe against two releases of the same report at the same moment: claiming is a
copy and a delete on a plain mapping, not an atomic move, so one interleaving
leaves a claim on a report the other release already sent, and the next
[`recover_claimed()`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.recover_claimed) sends it again. Serialise releases of one report.

* **Return type:**
  [`SinkResult`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.base.html.md#heed.sinks.base.SinkResult)

### heed.review_url(page_id, base_url=None)

The shareable link of a page: the base URL with the id as its fragment.

```pycon
>>> review_url("abc", "https://apps.example/review")
'https://apps.example/review/#abc'
>>> review_url("abc", "")  # no base URL: the fragment alone
'#abc'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### heed.roadmap(items)

Items still to come, started first; most-voted first within each stage.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`PublicItem`](_autosummary/heed.board.html.md#heed.board.PublicItem)]

### heed.screenshot_url_resolver(base_url, signer, , ref_pattern=re.compile('[0-9a-f]{32}\\\\.(?:png|jpg|webp)'))

A `GitHubIssuesSink(screenshot_url=...)` callable: the report’s first image

### heed.sinks_by_origin(sinks, , default=None)

A resolver from an `{origin: sink}` mapping (origins compared normalized).

Unknown origins resolve to `default`; with no default they resolve to None, and
the router refuses them.

```pycon
>>> from heed.sinks import StoreSink
>>> a = StoreSink({})
>>> resolve = sinks_by_origin({"https://a.example": a})
>>> resolve("HTTPS://A.example/") is a, resolve("https://b.example")
(True, None)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Sink`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.base.html.md#heed.sinks.base.Sink)]]

### heed.strip_image(data, media_type)

Keep only what renders the image; truncate at its end. Pure Python.

Raises `ValueError` when `data` is not a well-formed `media_type` image, or
one too costly to decode (over `MAX_JPEG_SCANS` scans, `_MAX_PARTS` parts).

* **Return type:**
  [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)

### heed.token_moderator(token, , also=None)

A moderator check that needs a secret the owner types in, not a login.

On an origin shared with other apps, a session cookie is ambient authority: any
script running there while the owner is logged in can call the API *as* the owner.
A secret in a request header is not ambient (the review page keeps it in memory,
never in storage), so such a script can neither delete comments nor post badged as
the owner. `also` (e.g. [`email_moderator()`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.email_moderator)) is required too, when given.

Use a random token (`secrets.token_urlsafe(24)`). This raises the bar, it is not a
wall: a hostile script on the same origin can still open the review page in a frame
and hook it before the owner types the token, or phish with its own prompt. A
dedicated origin for the review app is the real fix.

```pycon
>>> from types import SimpleNamespace as NS
>>> check = token_moderator("s3cret-token-value")
>>> check(NS(headers={"X-Heed-Moderator-Token": "s3cret-token-value"}))
True
>>> check(NS(headers={}))
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`Request`], [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)]

### heed.triage(report, , llm=None, labels=('ui', 'performance', 'crash', 'data-loss', 'security', 'accessibility', 'docs', 'auth', 'mobile'))

Propose a triage for `report`: by `llm` when given, else by keywords.

A model that raises or answers badly never fails the call: the safe default
(`fallback=True`) comes back instead.

* **Return type:**
  [`Triage`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.Triage)

### heed.widget_contract(config=None)

What the widget sends and the limits it must respect (from heed’s SSOT).

`config` supplies the server-configurable names (honeypot, bot token field) and
the screenshot cap; their defaults are what the widget assumes unless an embedder
overrides them.

```pycon
>>> widget_contract()["categories"]
['bug', 'feature', 'question', 'other']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

# _autosummary/heed.images.html.md

# heed.images

Neutralise uploaded screenshots before they are stored (issue #15).

Magic-byte sniffing ([`heed.security.sniff_image_type()`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.sniff_image_type)) proves a file *starts* like
a PNG, JPEG or WebP. It says nothing about the rest: a polyglot can carry a valid image
header followed by HTML, a ZIP, or a script, and EXIF/XMP metadata can carry GPS
coordinates. A sanitizer rewrites the accepted bytes to cut that down.

Sanitizers are `(data, media_type) -> bytes` callables that raise `ValueError` on a
malformed or refused image, looked up by name in `image_sanitizers`:

- `"auto"` (default): `"reencode"` when Pillow is installed, else `"strip"` (with
  a warning at startup).
- `"reencode"`: `strip` first (structure and cost checks), then decode and re-save
  the first frame with Pillow (`pip install heed[images]`). Only freshly encoded
  pixels are stored: no metadata, comments, extra frames or trailing data. At most
  `max_concurrent` re-encodes run at once; beyond that [`SanitizerBusy`](_autosummary/heed.images.html.md#heed.images.SanitizerBusy) is
  raised (the router answers 503).
- `"strip"`: pure Python, no dependency. Walks the container, keeps an allow-list of
  chunks/segments (each length-checked where the format fixes it), rejects unknown
  JPEG markers, and truncates at the end marker. Trailing payloads, metadata (EXIF, XMP,
  ICC, text chunks, comments) and animation are gone; the \*\*compressed pixel data is
  kept as sent\*\*, so attacker-chosen bytes can survive inside it.
- `"none"`: store the bytes as received (explicit opt-out).

Neither rewrite makes a stored file safe to serve on its own (even re-encoded pixel data
can hold attacker-chosen byte runs), so attachments must also be served with
[`heed.security.attachment_headers()`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.attachment_headers).

```pycon
>>> png = _tiny_png() + b"<html><script>alert(1)</script>"
>>> clean = strip_image(png, "image/png")
>>> clean == _tiny_png(), b"<html>" in clean
(True, False)
```

### heed.images.reencode_image(data, media_type, , max_pixels=8500000)

Strip `data`, then decode it and save its first frame afresh, same format.

Images over `max_pixels` are refused before any pixel is decoded (a small file can
declare a huge canvas). Nothing but pixels (and PNG palette transparency) is carried
over: no comment, EXIF, ICC profile or other metadata. Raises `ValueError` on a
malformed, oversized or too costly image.

* **Return type:**
  [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)

### heed.images.strip_image(data, media_type)

Keep only what renders the image; truncate at its end. Pure Python.

Raises `ValueError` when `data` is not a well-formed `media_type` image, or
one too costly to decode (over `MAX_JPEG_SCANS` scans, `_MAX_PARTS` parts).

* **Return type:**
  [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)


# _autosummary/heed.ingest.html.md

# heed.ingest

The ingest layer — build a Report from a submission and route it to a sink.

`process_submission` is the pure, framework-free core (dependency-injected sink,
stores, clock, id generator) so it is unit-testable without a server. `make_router`
wraps it in a FastAPI `APIRouter` you can run standalone (`make_app`) or
`include_router` into an enlace app. Identity is anonymous by default; pass a
`user_dependency` to bind identity when an auth layer (e.g. enlace_auth) is present.

The router treats every request as hostile (see `security.py` and issue #5). Checks
run cheapest-first so abuse is rejected before it costs anything: CORS preflight →
origin allow-list → per-IP rate limit (both before `user_dependency`) → body-size cap
(streamed, before parsing) → form limits → honeypot → bot gate → per-origin rate limit
→ model validation → screenshot sniffing → screenshot sanitizing (`images.py`: only
the image survives, so polyglot payloads and EXIF/GPS metadata are never stored).

#### NOTE
this module does not `from __future__ import annotations` — FastAPI resolves
route-handler annotations against module globals, so the request/response types are
imported at module level.

### Module Attributes

| [`THREAD_POOL_KINDS`](_autosummary/heed.ingest.html.md#heed.ingest.THREAD_POOL_KINDS)   | Kinds of blocking call the router runs off the event loop, each in its own pool sized by `HeedConfig.<kind>_threads`.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`make_app`](_autosummary/heed.ingest.html.md#heed.ingest.make_app)(sink, \*[, config, ...])               | A standalone FastAPI app serving the heed router under `prefix`.              |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`make_router`](_autosummary/heed.ingest.html.md#heed.ingest.make_router)(sink, \*[, config, ...])            | Build a FastAPI APIRouter exposing `POST /report` (and its CORS preflight).   |
| [`process_submission`](_autosummary/heed.ingest.html.md#heed.ingest.process_submission)(submission, sink, \*[, ...]) | Enrich `submission` into a Report, store any screenshot, and route to `sink`. |
| [`read_capped_body`](_autosummary/heed.ingest.html.md#heed.ingest.read_capped_body)(request, \*, max_bytes)        | Read the request body, or return None as soon as it exceeds `max_bytes`.      |

### heed.ingest.THREAD_POOL_KINDS *= ('limiter', 'bot_verify', 'reencode', 'delivery')*

Kinds of blocking call the router runs off the event loop, each in its own pool
sized by `HeedConfig.<kind>_threads`.

### heed.ingest.make_app(sink, , config=None, attachment_store=None, prefix='/heed', serve_widget=True, \*\*router_kwargs)

A standalone FastAPI app serving the heed router under `prefix`.

With `serve_widget` (the default) it also serves the built widget at
`{prefix}/widget/{file}` (see [`heed.widget`](_autosummary/heed.widget.html.md#module-heed.widget)), so one host both hands out the
script and receives its reports.

* **Return type:**
  `FastAPI`

### heed.ingest.make_router(sink, \*, config=None, attachment_store=None, rate_limiter=None, origin_rate_limiter=None, bot_verifier=None, user_dependency=None, resolve_sink=None, moderator=None, holding_sink=None, image_sanitizer=None, redactor=<function redact_text>)

Build a FastAPI APIRouter exposing `POST /report` (and its CORS preflight).

Run standalone via [`make_app()`](_autosummary/heed.ingest.html.md#heed.ingest.make_app), or `include_router` it into an enlace app.
Provide `user_dependency` (a FastAPI dependency returning a user id or None) to
bind identity when an auth layer like enlace_auth is present.

Hardening defaults come from `config`; any piece can be injected instead:
`rate_limiter` (per client IP), `origin_rate_limiter` (per Origin) and
`bot_verifier` (by default built from `config.bot_secret`, i.e. off until a
secret is configured) and `image_sanitizer` (by default from
`config.screenshot_sanitizer`: re-encode with Pillow, else a pure-Python strip).
Opt-in console/network capture (`config.accept_console`/`accept_network`) is
masked by `redactor` before any sink sees it; a field the config does not accept
is never parsed.

Routing is decided server-side, never by the browser: `resolve_sink` maps the
validated origin to that site’s sink (`sink` is then the fallback and may be
None; an origin resolving to no sink gets 403). `moderator` may hold reports in
`holding_sink` (required with a moderator) or reject them; see `routing.py`.

* **Return type:**
  `APIRouter`

### heed.ingest.process_submission(submission, sink, \*, origin='', user=None, screenshot=None, screenshot_media_type='image/png', attachment_store=None, config=None, id_gen=<function new_report_id>, clock=<function utcnow>, moderator=<function accept_all>, holding_sink=None, redactor=<function redact_text>)

Enrich `submission` into a Report, store any screenshot, and route to `sink`.

Returns the (report, sink-result) pair. The server owns id/created_at/identity/
origin/status — never the client. Opt-in capture (console/network) is dropped
unless enabled in `config`, and what is kept is passed through `redactor`
(personal data and secrets masked, see `redact.py`) whatever the widget did.
`moderator` decides first: `hold` sends the report
(status `held`) to `holding_sink` instead, `reject` drops it (status
`declined`).

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`Report`](_autosummary/heed.base.html.md#heed.base.Report), [`SinkResult`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.base.html.md#heed.sinks.base.SinkResult)]

### *async* heed.ingest.read_capped_body(request, , max_bytes)

Read the request body, or return None as soon as it exceeds `max_bytes`.

Checks `Content-Length` first, then counts streamed bytes (a chunked request
has no length header), so an oversized body is never buffered whole.

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)]


# _autosummary/heed.mcp.html.md

# heed.mcp

The feedback queue as an MCP server (`pip install 'heed[mcp]'`) (#8).

Each [`FeedbackQueue`](_autosummary/heed.queue.html.md#heed.queue.FeedbackQueue) operation becomes one MCP tool through
`py2mcp` (imported only here, on use), so an agent such as Claude Code can list,
read, triage, deduplicate, file and close reports. The tools are the queue’s own
functions, the same ones any other surface calls.

Run it over a report directory:

```default
python -m heed.mcp /path/to/reports        # stdio transport
```

The report text the tools return was written by anonymous users: an agent reading it
must treat it as data, never as instructions (the server says so in its
instructions).

### Functions

| [`main`](_autosummary/heed.mcp.html.md#heed.mcp.main)([argv])                                | `python -m heed.mcp REPORT_DIR`: serve the queue over stdio.      |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`mk_feedback_mcp`](_autosummary/heed.mcp.html.md#heed.mcp.mk_feedback_mcp)([store, rootdir, llm, ...]) | A FastMCP server whose tools are the feedback queue's operations. |

### heed.mcp.main(argv=None)

`python -m heed.mcp REPORT_DIR`: serve the queue over stdio.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### heed.mcp.mk_feedback_mcp(store=None, , rootdir=None, llm=None, confirm=None, name='heed feedback queue')

A FastMCP server whose tools are the feedback queue’s operations.

Give the report `store` itself, or the `rootdir` of a report directory.

* **Return type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)


# _autosummary/heed.queue.html.md

# heed.queue

The feedback queue as plain functions: list, get, triage, dedup, create, close (#8).

One set of core functions over a report store (the `MutableMapping` a
[`StoreSink`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.store.html.md#heed.sinks.store.StoreSink) writes, e.g.
[`heed.storage.make_report_store()`](_autosummary/heed.storage.html.md#heed.storage.make_report_store)),
shared by every surface: [`heed.mcp`](_autosummary/heed.mcp.html.md#module-heed.mcp) exposes them as MCP tools, and a CLI or an
admin page would call the same ones. Arguments are flat and results are JSON-ready
dicts, so a tool layer adds nothing but transport.

`create` goes through [`heed.ingest.process_submission()`](_autosummary/heed.ingest.html.md#heed.ingest.process_submission), the same path as a
widget submission (validation, enrichment), so an agent cannot write a report the
HTTP router would not.

```pycon
>>> q = FeedbackQueue({})
>>> rid = q.create("Export to CSV fails", body="the button errors")["id"]
>>> [r["title"] for r in q.list()]
['Export to CSV fails']
>>> q.triage(rid)["severity"]
'high'
>>> q.close(rid, status="completed")["status"]
'completed'
```

# _autosummary/heed.redact.html.md

# heed.redact

Redaction of personal data and secrets in captured console and network entries.

Opt-in capture (heed#7) sends console messages and request URLs, and both routinely
carry things nobody meant to report: an e-mail address in a log line, a session token
in a query string, a bearer header someone logged while debugging. The widget masks
them before anything leaves the page (redact *before* capture); the server applies
the same rules again here, because the ingest endpoint is public and a client can send
anything. The rules are deliberately greedy: a lost hex string costs a little
debugging, a leaked token costs an incident.

The widget’s `mask.ts` mirrors these rules; keep the two in step.

```pycon
>>> redact_text("login failed for ana@example.com with token=abc123")
'login failed for [email] with token=[redacted]'
>>> redact_url("https://u:pw@app.example/a/b?session=xyz&page=2#top")
'https://app.example/a/b?session=[redacted]&page=[redacted]'
```

### Functions

| [`redact_console`](_autosummary/heed.redact.html.md#heed.redact.redact_console)(entries, \*[, redactor])   | Console entries with their level, message and source redacted.                                                            |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`redact_network`](_autosummary/heed.redact.html.md#heed.redact.redact_network)(entries, \*[, redactor])   | Network entries with their method redacted and their URL stripped of credentials, query values and id-like path segments. |
| [`redact_text`](_autosummary/heed.redact.html.md#heed.redact.redact_text)(text)                         | Replace personal data and secrets in `text` by placeholders.                                                              |
| [`redact_url`](_autosummary/heed.redact.html.md#heed.redact.redact_url)(url, \*[, redactor])           | `url` without credentials, fragment or query values (keys are kept).                                                      |

### heed.redact.redact_console(entries, \*, redactor=<function redact_text>)

Console entries with their level, message and source redacted.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`LogEntry`](_autosummary/heed.base.html.md#heed.base.LogEntry)]

### heed.redact.redact_network(entries, \*, redactor=<function redact_text>)

Network entries with their method redacted and their URL stripped of
credentials, query values and id-like path segments.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`NetEntry`](_autosummary/heed.base.html.md#heed.base.NetEntry)]

### heed.redact.redact_text(text)

Replace personal data and secrets in `text` by placeholders.

```pycon
>>> redact_text("Authorization: Bearer abc.def.ghi")
'Authorization: [redacted]'
>>> redact_text("paid with 4111 1111 1111 1111, order 1234567890123")
'paid with [card], order 1234567890123'
>>> redact_text('{"password": "hunter2", "user": "ana"}')
'{"password": "[redacted]", "user": "ana"}'
```

URLs in the text are masked like request URLs ([`redact_url()`](_autosummary/heed.redact.html.md#heed.redact.redact_url)) first:

```pycon
>>> redact_text("callback https://app.example/cb?code=4/0AbC&state=x failed")
'callback https://app.example/cb?code=[redacted]&state=[redacted] failed'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### heed.redact.redact_url(url, \*, redactor=<function redact_text>)

`url` without credentials, fragment or query values (keys are kept).

Path segments that look like ids (all digits, or 12+ characters with a digit) or
handles (`@name`) are replaced, path parameters dropped, and the rest of each
segment redacted as text.

```pycon
>>> redact_url("/api/users/ana@example.com?q=1")
'/api/users/[email]?q=[redacted]'
>>> redact_url("https://app.example/reset/9f8e7d6c5b4a3f2e;jsessionid=X/42")
'https://app.example/reset/[id]/[id]'
>>> redact_url("https://app.example/r/AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOpQr%2Fx/eyJhbGci.eyJzdWIi.sigpart")
'https://app.example/r/[id]/[id]'
>>> redact_url("mailto:ana@example.com")
'mailto:[redacted]'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/heed.review.html.md

# heed.review

Review pages: media (a video, audio, images) with a comment thread under it.

Publish one or more media files under a title and get a link; whoever has the link
watches the media and reads and adds comments (a name per comment, optionally pinned
to a moment in the video), on every visit, without an account. The owner deletes
comments, over HTTP when `is_moderator` says so or from the CLI. On an origin shared
with other apps, use `token_moderator` (a typed-in secret) rather than a login alone:
a login is ambient, so any script on that origin acts as the owner (#74).

The link is a **capability**: the page id is 128 random bits and travels in the URL
*fragment* (`https://host/review/#<id>`), so the link itself is never sent in a
request or a `Referer` (the API calls the page makes do carry the id in their
paths, so the host’s access logs see it). Without the id a page, its media and its
thread are all 404s. On top of that the thread endpoint is rate-limited per IP and per
thread, capped per thread, size-capped, and has a honeypot (see [`heed.threads`](_autosummary/heed.threads.html.md#module-heed.threads)).

Layout of the data root (one folder; ADR-0024’s S3 layout mirrors it key for key):

```default
pages/<id>.json            the page: title, note, media list, created_at
media/<id>/<name>          the media files, served with byte ranges (seekable)
comments/<id>/<cid>.json   the thread (heed.threads)
access/<id>.json           optional password, expiry, revoke (heed.review_access);
                           no file means open: back this folder up too
```

Python:

```default
>>> import tempfile
>>> root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
>>> clip = os.path.join(root, "cut1.mp4"); _ = open(clip, "wb").write(b"\0" * 10)
>>> page = publish_review([clip], title="Plot car, cut 1", rootdir=root)
>>> [m.name for m in page.media], len(page.id)
(['cut1.mp4'], 22)
>>> url = review_url(page.id, "https://apps.example/review/")
>>> url == "https://apps.example/review/#" + page.id
True
```

The review API (and, with `serve_shell`, the page at `/`).

Routes: `GET /pages/{id}`, `GET /pages/{id}/media/{name}` (byte ranges;
`?download=1` serves it as an attachment, so a phone saves the file),
`GET|POST /threads/{id}`, `DELETE /threads/{id}/{comment}` (moderators),
`GET /ui/review.{js,css}`. There is deliberately no HTTP listing of pages:
it would hand every capability to any script running as the owner (the CLI’s
`ls` lists them).

A page given a password, an expiry or a revoke ([`publish_review()`](_autosummary/heed.review.html.md#heed.review.publish_review),
`heed review revoke`) is gated by `gate` (a `ReviewGate`, built over
`rootdir` with `trusted_proxies` by default): 401 until `POST
/pages/{id}/unlock` `{"password": ...}` sets a cookie, 410 once expired, 404
once revoked. Pages with no such record are open, as ever.

* **Return type:**
  `FastAPI`

# _autosummary/heed.review_access.html.md

# heed.review_access

Access control for review pages: an optional password, expiry and revoke.

A review page is a capability (its 128-bit id), and by default stays one forever. This
module adds what a link sent to a client needs, on top of [caplinks](https://github.com/i2mint/caplinks) (the optional `heed[gate]` extra): a password,
an expiry, and a revoke, kept as one record per page under `<root>/access/<id>.json`.

A page **with no record is open**, exactly as before; a page with one is gated. So
nothing changes for existing pages, and `caplinks` is only imported when a record
exists or one is being written (a gated page whose `caplinks` is missing answers 503,
never open).

Python:

```default
>>> import tempfile
>>> root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
>>> page_id = "A" * 22
>>> rec = set_access(root, page_id, password="open sesame", expires="7d")
>>> rec["protected"]
True
>>> revoke_access(root, page_id)["revoked"] is not None
True
```

HTTP: [`ReviewGate`](_autosummary/heed.review_access.html.md#heed.review_access.ReviewGate) is what [`heed.review.make_review_app()`](_autosummary/heed.review.html.md#heed.review.make_review_app) consults. A gated
page answers 401 until `POST /pages/{id}/unlock` with the password sets a cookie
(HMAC keyed by the stored hash, so a new password or a revoke ends every open session);
an expired page answers 410, a revoked one 404. Wrong passwords are limited per client
per page, and a page that takes too many wrong ones from everyone is locked for a while.

### Module Attributes

| [`COOKIE_ID_HEX`](_autosummary/heed.review_access.html.md#heed.review_access.COOKIE_ID_HEX)          | hex chars of the page id's hash in the cookie name (the id itself is the capability and must not travel to other apps on the origin)   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DFLT_MAX_ATTEMPTS`](_autosummary/heed.review_access.html.md#heed.review_access.DFLT_MAX_ATTEMPTS)      | password tries one client gets on one page per window                                                                                  |
| [`DFLT_MAX_PAGE_FAILURES`](_autosummary/heed.review_access.html.md#heed.review_access.DFLT_MAX_PAGE_FAILURES) | wrong passwords one page takes from everyone per window before it locks                                                                |
| [`DFLT_UNLOCK_MAX_AGE_S`](_autosummary/heed.review_access.html.md#heed.review_access.DFLT_UNLOCK_MAX_AGE_S)  | how long an unlock cookie lasts (never past the page's expiry)                                                                         |

### Functions

| [`revoke_access`](_autosummary/heed.review_access.html.md#heed.review_access.revoke_access)(rootdir, page_id)                   | End page `page_id` for every visitor: it answers 404 from now on.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`set_access`](_autosummary/heed.review_access.html.md#heed.review_access.set_access)(rootdir, page_id, \*[, password, ...]) | Gate page `page_id` (creating its access record, or updating it).   |

### Classes

| [`ReviewGate`](_autosummary/heed.review_access.html.md#heed.review_access.ReviewGate)(rootdir, \*[, trusted_proxies, ...])   | The HTTP side of the gate: refuse, unlock, and limit password tries.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### heed.review_access.COOKIE_ID_HEX *= 16*

hex chars of the page id’s hash in the cookie name (the id itself is the capability
and must not travel to other apps on the origin)

### heed.review_access.DFLT_MAX_ATTEMPTS *= 10*

password tries one client gets on one page per window

### heed.review_access.DFLT_MAX_PAGE_FAILURES *= 30*

### *class* heed.review_access.ReviewGate(rootdir, \*, trusted_proxies=(), rate_limiter=None, page_failure_limiter=None, unlock_max_age_s=604800, lock_s=300.0, clock=<built-in function monotonic>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The HTTP side of the gate: refuse, unlock, and limit password tries.

`rate_limiter` counts every try of one client on one page;
`page_failure_limiter` counts the wrong passwords a page takes from everyone and,
past its limit, locks the page’s unlock for `lock_s` seconds. Both are anything
with `allow(key) -> bool` (heed’s Redis limiter fits). Behind a reverse proxy set
`trusted_proxies`.

#### check(request, page_id)

Raise `HTTPException` (404 revoked, 410 expired, 401 locked) unless the
page is open to `request`; an ungated page always is.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### *async* unlock(request, page_id)

Check the posted password; set the unlock cookie when it is right.

* **Return type:**
  `Response`

### heed.review_access.revoke_access(rootdir, page_id)

End page `page_id` for every visitor: it answers 404 from now on.

A page with no access record is first gated (so it can be revoked), then revoked.

### heed.review_access.set_access(rootdir, page_id, , password=None, expires=None)

Gate page `page_id` (creating its access record, or updating it).

`password` (at least 8 characters) and `expires` (`"7d"`, `"2026-11-01"`,
an ISO timestamp, `"never"`) are changed only when given, so
`set_access(root, id, expires="30d")` keeps the password. Returns the record
without the hash. A revoked page stays revoked (`KeyError`).


# _autosummary/heed.routing.html.md

# heed.routing

Where a report goes: server-side site resolution and moderation (holding state).

Two seams, both decided on the server, never by the browser:

- **Site resolution**: a `SinkResolver` maps the *validated* request origin to
  the sink for that site (e.g. which GitHub repo). The widget never names a target, so
  a visitor cannot redirect reports into someone else’s tracker.
  [`sinks_by_origin()`](_autosummary/heed.routing.html.md#heed.routing.sinks_by_origin) builds one from a plain mapping.
- **Moderation**: a `Moderator` looks at a server-enriched report and returns a
  [`Verdict`](_autosummary/heed.routing.html.md#heed.routing.Verdict). `hold` parks the report in a holding sink (status `held`)
  > until a human releases it with [`release_held()`](_autosummary/heed.routing.html.md#heed.routing.release_held); `reject` drops it.

  [`accept_all()`](_autosummary/heed.routing.html.md#heed.routing.accept_all) is the default, [`hold_all()`](_autosummary/heed.routing.html.md#heed.routing.hold_all) gives full pre-moderation, and
  [`make_heuristic_moderator()`](_autosummary/heed.routing.html.md#heed.routing.make_heuristic_moderator) holds link floods and blocked terms.

### Module Attributes

| [`CLAIM_PREFIX`](_autosummary/heed.routing.html.md#heed.routing.CLAIM_PREFIX)   | Prefix of the keys reports are claimed under, in the holding store itself, while they are being released (when no separate `claimed_store` is given).   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`fold_text`](_autosummary/heed.routing.html.md#heed.routing.fold_text)(text)                                   | Normalise text for matching: NFKC, drop format chars (zero-width), casefold. |

| [`recover_claimed`](_autosummary/heed.routing.html.md#heed.routing.recover_claimed)(\*, holding_store[, ...])         | Return every claimed report to holding, and the ids returned.                |
