### heed.routing.accept_all(report)

The default moderator: everything goes straight to the sink.

* **Return type:**
  [`Verdict`](_autosummary/heed.routing.html.md#heed.routing.Verdict)

### heed.routing.chain_moderators(\*moderators)

Combine moderators; the most severe verdict wins (reject > hold > accept).

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Report`](_autosummary/heed.base.html.md#heed.base.Report)], [`Verdict`](_autosummary/heed.routing.html.md#heed.routing.Verdict)]

### heed.routing.discard_held(report_id, , holding_store, attachment_store=None)

Delete a held report for good, with its attachments (e.g. a screenshot).

The report leaves holding first, so a release that took it meanwhile wins and this
raises `KeyError` before touching its attachments; a crash between the two steps
leaves an orphaned screenshot, never a report pointing at a deleted one. Raises
`KeyError` when `report_id` is not held. A report whose text no longer parses is
still deleted, but its attachments cannot be named and are left. Run it serialised
with [`release_held()`](_autosummary/heed.routing.html.md#heed.routing.release_held) for the same report.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### heed.routing.fold_text(text)

Normalise text for matching: NFKC, drop format chars (zero-width), casefold.

Defeats fullwidth letters and zero-width splitting; it does not map cross-script
look-alikes (e.g. Cyrillic “а”), which needs a confusables table.

```pycon
>>> fold_text("ＣＡＳ​INO")
'casino'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### heed.routing.hold_all(report)

Full pre-moderation: every report waits for a human.

* **Return type:**
  [`Verdict`](_autosummary/heed.routing.html.md#heed.routing.Verdict)

### heed.routing.make_heuristic_moderator(, max_links=3, blocked_terms=(), on_blocked_term=Verdict.hold)

Hold reports with more than `max_links` links or any of `blocked_terms`.

Cheap, dependency-free spam signals. Holding (not rejecting) is the default so a
false positive costs a human click, not a lost report.

```pycon
>>> mod = make_heuristic_moderator(max_links=1, blocked_terms=["casino"])
>>> from heed.base import Identity
>>> def r(body): return Report(title="t", body=body, identity=Identity(anon_id="a"))
>>> [mod(r(b)).value for b in ["ok", "http://a http://b", "best CASINO"]]
['accept', 'hold', 'hold']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Report`](_autosummary/heed.base.html.md#heed.base.Report)], [`Verdict`](_autosummary/heed.routing.html.md#heed.routing.Verdict)]

### heed.routing.recover_claimed(\*, holding_store, claimed_store=None, stale_after=None, clock=<built-in function time>)

Return every claimed report to holding, and the ids returned.

A claim outlives its [`release_held()`](_autosummary/heed.routing.html.md#heed.routing.release_held) only if the process died mid-release
(the sink may or may not have accepted the report, so a recovered report may be
sent twice – never zero times). Pass the same `claimed_store` as to
[`release_held()`](_autosummary/heed.routing.html.md#heed.routing.release_held).

An in-flight release’s claim looks the same as a stranded one. With one process,
call this when no release is running (e.g. at startup) and leave `stale_after`
unset: every claim is recovered. With several workers, one worker’s startup can
overlap another’s release, so pass `stale_after` (seconds; longer than any sink
call can take plus the clock skew between workers, e.g. `600`): only claims older
than that are recovered (and claims stamped further ahead than that, by a clock
running fast). Claims made before claim keys carried a time count as stale. A
release whose claim is recovered anyway puts the report back in holding and fails.
Beside a dedicated claims store, `claimed--` claims an older heed left in holding
are recovered too (which lists holding once).

Only a valid report (whose own id matches its claim key) is ever written to
holding, and a valid holding copy is never replaced: a claim whose report is
intact in holding is just dropped (even a torn one), and one whose holding copy
is torn or missing restores it. Otherwise a claim that is not a valid report is
left in place, and not returned.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### heed.routing.release_held(report_id, \*, holding_store, sink=None, resolve_sink=None, claimed_store=None, clock=<built-in function time>)

Release a held report: route it on and remove it from holding.

`holding_store` is the store behind the holding sink (a `StoreSink`’s
`.store`). The destination is `sink`, or — for a multi-site backend — the sink
`resolve_sink` gives for the report’s own origin (pass exactly one).

The report is claimed before submitting, so a second release while the first is in
flight finds nothing to send. Claiming *moves* it: it is written under a claim key
of its own (`<id>--<time>-<token>`) in the claims store and only then deleted
from holding. The claims store is `claimed_store` if given, else the one a
`make_holding_store` store carries, else (legacy) `holding_store` itself under a
`claimed--` prefix – which makes every release list the whole holding store.
If the sink fails the report is put back in holding; a release only ever
deletes its own claim, and only once the sink has accepted the report or it is
back in holding. So a crash at any point leaves the report in holding, in the
claims, or in both – never lost – and [`recover_claimed()`](_autosummary/heed.routing.html.md#heed.routing.recover_claimed) returns stranded
claims to holding. A report with a claim is not released again until then.

Not safe against two releases of the same report at the same moment: claiming is a
copy and a delete on a plain mapping, not an atomic move, so one interleaving
leaves a claim on a report the other release already sent, and the next
[`recover_claimed()`](_autosummary/heed.routing.html.md#heed.routing.recover_claimed) sends it again. Serialise releases of one report.

* **Return type:**
  [`SinkResult`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.base.html.md#heed.sinks.base.SinkResult)

### heed.routing.sinks_by_origin(sinks, , default=None)

A resolver from an `{origin: sink}` mapping (origins compared normalized).

Unknown origins resolve to `default`; with no default they resolve to None, and
the router refuses them.

```pycon
>>> from heed.sinks import StoreSink
>>> a = StoreSink({})
>>> resolve = sinks_by_origin({"https://a.example": a})
>>> resolve("HTTPS://A.example/") is a, resolve("https://b.example")
(True, None)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Sink`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.base.html.md#heed.sinks.base.Sink)]]


# _autosummary/heed.security.html.md

# heed.security

Public-endpoint hardening (the ingest endpoint is unauthenticated and hostile).

Everything here is a small function or a strategy behind a protocol, so the router
composes them and deployments swap implementations without touching it:

- **Origins / CORS**: [`origin_allowed()`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.origin_allowed), [`cors_headers()`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.cors_headers),
  [`preflight_headers()`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.preflight_headers).
- **Client identity for rate limiting**: [`client_ip()`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.client_ip) (honours
  `X-Forwarded-For` only from trusted proxies).
- **Rate limiting**: the [`RateLimiter`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.RateLimiter) protocol, an in-memory default
  ([`InMemoryRateLimiter`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.InMemoryRateLimiter), per process) and [`RedisRateLimiter`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.RedisRateLimiter) (shared
  across workers), looked up by name via [`make_rate_limiter()`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.make_rate_limiter).
- **Bot gate**: the [`BotVerifier`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.BotVerifier) protocol and [`SiteverifyBotVerifier`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.SiteverifyBotVerifier)
  for Cloudflare Turnstile / hCaptcha, built by [`make_bot_verifier()`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.make_bot_verifier) only when a
  secret is configured (off otherwise).
- **Attachments**: [`sniff_image_type()`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.sniff_image_type) checks screenshot magic bytes (and
  `images.py` rewrites them); [`attachment_headers()`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.attachment_headers) is how to serve them.

### Module Attributes

| [`ATTACHMENT_RESPONSE_HEADERS`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.ATTACHMENT_RESPONSE_HEADERS)   | Response headers for serving a stored attachment, whatever its bytes contain: never sniffed as another type, never allowed to run script or load anything, never cached by shared caches.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* heed.security.BotVerifier(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

Verify a human-challenge token server-side; True means “looks human”.

### *class* heed.security.InMemoryRateLimiter(\*, max_per_window=30, window_seconds=60.0, max_keys=100000, clock=<built-in function monotonic>)

Bases: `_WindowKnobs`, `SlidingWindowLimiter`

Sliding-window, in-memory limiter. Per process — NOT shared across workers.

Fine for a single-worker deployment; with several workers each one counts alone,
so the effective limit is multiplied. Use [`RedisRateLimiter`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.RedisRateLimiter) there. The
number of tracked keys is bounded (`max_keys`, least-recently-seen evicted) so a
flood of distinct keys cannot exhaust memory.

### *class* heed.security.RateLimiter(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

Decide whether a request keyed by `key` (e.g. client IP) is allowed now.

### *class* heed.security.RedisRateLimiter(client, \*, max_per_window=30, window_seconds=60.0, namespace='heed:rl', fallback=None, max_keys=100000, clock=<built-in function time>)

Bases: `_WindowKnobs`, `RedisLimiter`

Fixed-window limiter in Redis — one count shared by every worker and host.

`client` is any redis-py compatible client (injected; tests use a fake). When
Redis errors, the request is decided by `fallback` (a per-process in-memory
limiter by default), so an outage degrades protection instead of either dropping
all feedback or removing the limit. `from_url()` builds the client from a
`redis://` URL (needs the `[redis]` extra).

After a Redis error the fallback alone decides for `retry_seconds` (5 s by
default) before Redis is tried again, so a hung Redis costs one socket timeout
per interval, not one per request; one warning per outage is logged, on the
`enlace.ratelimit` logger. An `allow`-only `fallback` is wrapped to answer
`acquire` too, so `.fallback` is then that wrapper (its `.limiter` is
yours). Counters are named `{namespace}:{window}:{key}:{window number}`.

#### install_hint *= "pip install 'heed[redis]'"*

Shown when the optional `redis` client is not installed.

### *class* heed.security.SiteverifyBotVerifier(secret, \*, verify_url='https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify', expected_hostnames=None, timeout=5.0, max_token_chars=4096, http_post=<function \_urllib_post_form>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Turnstile / hCaptcha verification (both speak the same siteverify protocol).

Fails closed: a missing token, a network error, or a malformed answer all verify
as False. `expected_hostnames`, when given, also rejects tokens solved on
another site. `http_post` is injectable (tests never touch the network).

### heed.security.attachment_headers(media_type, , filename=None, cross_origin=False)

Headers for serving a stored screenshot (issue #15). Use them on every response
that returns attachment bytes, ideally from an origin separate from the app’s.

Only the image types heed accepts are served as themselves; anything else is sent as
an opaque download. Embedding is limited to the same site
(`Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-site`) unless `cross_origin=True`, which a
screenshot embedded elsewhere (e.g. in a GitHub issue) needs.

```pycon
>>> h = attachment_headers("image/png", filename="r1.png")
>>> h["Content-Type"], h["X-Content-Type-Options"], h["Content-Disposition"]
('image/png', 'nosniff', 'inline; filename="r1.png"')
>>> attachment_headers("text/html")["Content-Type"]
'application/octet-stream'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### heed.security.client_ip(peer, forwarded_for, , trusted_proxies=())

The client address to rate-limit on (`enlace.ratelimit.client_address()`).

`X-Forwarded-For` is attacker-controlled unless the direct peer is a trusted
proxy, so it is only consulted then — and read right-to-left, skipping trusted
hops, so a client cannot prepend a fake address. A hop that is not an address
stops the walk (the peer is used).

```pycon
>>> client_ip("10.0.0.1", "6.6.6.6, 1.2.3.4", trusted_proxies=["10.0.0.0/8"])
'1.2.3.4'
>>> client_ip("5.5.5.5", "1.2.3.4")  # untrusted peer: header ignored
'5.5.5.5'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### heed.security.cors_headers(origin, allowed, , allow_credentials=False)

CORS response headers for `origin`, or `{}` when it is not allowed.

The request’s own origin is echoed (never `*`) so the response is correct with
or without credentials; `Vary: Origin` keeps shared caches honest.
`Retry-After` is exposed so the widget can tell a visitor when to retry.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### heed.security.make_bot_verifier(provider, secret, \*\*kwargs)

Return a verifier, or `None` (gate off) when no secret is configured.

`provider` defaults to `"turnstile"` when a secret is given.

* **Return type:**
  [`BotVerifier`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.BotVerifier) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### heed.security.make_rate_limiter(backend='memory', , max_per_window, window_seconds=60.0, namespace='ip', redis_url=None, max_keys=100000, redis_socket_timeout=0.5)

Build a limiter from the `rate_limiter_backends` registry by name.

* **Return type:**
  [`RateLimiter`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.RateLimiter)

### heed.security.normalize_origin(origin)

Canonical form of an origin for comparison (lower-case, no trailing slash).

```pycon
>>> normalize_origin("HTTPS://App.Example/")
'https://app.example'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### heed.security.origin_allowed(origin, allowed)

True if origin is permitted; `allowed=None` allows any (the dev default).

```pycon
>>> origin_allowed("https://a.example", ["https://a.example"])
True
>>> origin_allowed(None, ["https://a.example"])
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### heed.security.preflight_headers(origin, allowed, , allow_credentials=False, max_age_seconds=600, methods='POST, OPTIONS', request_headers=None)

Headers answering a CORS preflight, or `{}` when the origin is not allowed.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### heed.security.rate_limit_key(ip, , ipv6_prefix=64)

The bucket key for `ip`: IPv4 as-is, IPv6 grouped by its /`ipv6_prefix`.

One IPv6 host typically owns a whole /64, so per-address buckets are trivially
dodged by rotating addresses (`enlace.ratelimit.bucket_key()`).

```pycon
>>> rate_limit_key("2001:db8::1") == rate_limit_key("2001:db8::ffff")
True
>>> rate_limit_key("1.2.3.4")
'1.2.3.4'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### heed.security.sniff_image_type(data)

The media type of `data` from its magic bytes, or None if not an allowed image.

Never trust the client’s declared content type: an “image” might be HTML/SVG.

```pycon
>>> sniff_image_type(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n...")
'image/png'
>>> sniff_image_type(b"<svg onload=alert(1)>") is None
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)


# _autosummary/heed.serving.html.md

# heed.serving

Serve stored screenshots: a read-only route meant for its own origin (issue #19).

heed stores sanitized screenshots in the attachment store (`images.py`); a GitHub
issue can only show one through a URL (design.md §9). This module is that URL’s server:

- `AttachmentSigner` mints and checks signed URLs. Report ids are not secrets (the
  submit response, the report JSON, logs and holding stores all carry them), so by
  default a screenshot is served only with a valid HMAC signature, which only the
  backend can make — typically when a sink embeds the screenshot in an issue. Held or
  rejected reports’ screenshots therefore have no URL at all.
- `make_attachment_router` / `make_attachment_app` serve `GET <path>/<ref>` with
  `attachment_headers` on every response. Mount them on a dedicated origin (a
  subdomain such as `files.example.com`), never the app’s: `allowed_hosts` refuses
  any other `Host`.
- `screenshot_url_resolver` plugs the signer into
  `GitHubIssuesSink(screenshot_url=)`.

```pycon
>>> from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
>>> from heed.images import _tiny_png
>>> store = {"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.png": _tiny_png()}
>>> signer = AttachmentSigner("k" * 32)
>>> app = make_attachment_app(store, signer=signer, allowed_hosts=["testserver"])
>>> url = signer.url("/attachments", "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.png")
>>> r = TestClient(app).get(url)
>>> r.status_code, r.headers["content-type"], r.headers["x-content-type-options"]
(200, 'image/png', 'nosniff')
>>> TestClient(app).get("/attachments/0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.png").status_code
404
```

### Module Attributes

| [`DEFAULT_REF_PATTERN`](_autosummary/heed.serving.html.md#heed.serving.DEFAULT_REF_PATTERN)   | `{uuid4 hex}.{image extension}` (`process_submission`).   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| [`ANY_HOST`](_autosummary/heed.serving.html.md#heed.serving.ANY_HOST)              | the route answers on every host.                          |

### Functions

| [`make_attachment_app`](_autosummary/heed.serving.html.md#heed.serving.make_attachment_app)(attachment_store, ...)    | A standalone app serving only the attachment route (no docs, no OpenAPI): run it on the dedicated attachment origin.                |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`make_attachment_router`](_autosummary/heed.serving.html.md#heed.serving.make_attachment_router)(attachment_store, \*)  | A router serving `GET {path}/{ref}` from `attachment_store`, read-only.                                                             |
| [`screenshot_url_resolver`](_autosummary/heed.serving.html.md#heed.serving.screenshot_url_resolver)(base_url, signer, \*) | A `GitHubIssuesSink(screenshot_url=...)` callable: the report's first image attachment as a (signed) URL under `base_url`, or None. |

### Classes

| [`AttachmentSigner`](_autosummary/heed.serving.html.md#heed.serving.AttachmentSigner)(key, \*[, previous_keys, ...])   | Mint and check signed attachment URLs (HMAC-SHA256 over the ref and expiry).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### heed.serving.ANY_HOST *= '\*'*

the route answers on every host.

* **Type:**
  `allowed_hosts=ANY_HOST` (or `["*"]`)

### *class* heed.serving.AttachmentSigner(key, \*, previous_keys=(), ttl_seconds=None, clock=<built-in function time>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Mint and check signed attachment URLs (HMAC-SHA256 over the ref and expiry).

`ttl_seconds=None` (the default) signs URLs that never expire: a GitHub issue
keeps showing its screenshot, and access is revoked by deleting the attachment or
rotating the key. A ttl makes URLs expire, which suits links handed to people rather
than embedded in issues. `previous_keys` still verify (never sign), for rotation.

```pycon
>>> s = AttachmentSigner("k" * 32, ttl_seconds=60, clock=lambda: 1000)
>>> q = s.sign("ab.png")
>>> q["exp"], s.verify("ab.png", **q), s.verify("other.png", **q)
('1060', True, False)
>>> later = AttachmentSigner("k" * 32, ttl_seconds=60, clock=lambda: 2000)
>>> later.verify("ab.png", **q)
False
```

#### *classmethod* from_config(config, \*\*kwargs)

The signer `config` describes, or None if it has no signing key.

* **Return type:**
  [`AttachmentSigner`](_autosummary/heed.serving.html.md#heed.serving.AttachmentSigner) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### sign(ref)

The query parameters authorising `ref`: `sig`, and `exp` with a ttl.

* **Return type:**

#### url(base_url, ref)

`{base_url}/{ref}?...`: the signed URL of `ref` under `base_url`.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### verify(ref, , sig=None, exp=None)

Whether `sig` (and `exp`, if any) authorise `ref` right now.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### heed.serving.DEFAULT_REF_PATTERN *= re.compile('[0-9a-f]{32}\\\\.(?:png|jpg|webp)')*

`{uuid4 hex}.{image extension}` (`process_submission`).
Anything else is refused before the store is touched (no path tricks into a file
store).

* **Type:**
  Refs heed itself writes

### heed.serving.make_attachment_app(attachment_store, \*\*router_kwargs)

A standalone app serving only the attachment route (no docs, no OpenAPI): run it
on the dedicated attachment origin. Keyword arguments go to
`make_attachment_router`.

* **Return type:**
  `FastAPI`

### heed.serving.make_attachment_router(attachment_store, , config=None, signer=None, allow_unsigned=False, allowed_hosts=None, cross_origin=False, cache_control=None, max_bytes=None, path='/attachments', ref_pattern=re.compile('[0-9a-f]{32}\\\\.(?:png|jpg|webp)'))

A router serving `GET {path}/{ref}` from `attachment_store`, read-only.

Every response that returns bytes carries `attachment_headers`; the bytes are
re-sniffed, and anything that is not the image its extension names is sent as an
opaque download. A missing, malformed, unsigned or expired ref is the same bare 404,
so the route is no oracle for which reports exist; a wrong `Host` is a 421 (a
deployment error worth seeing). Behind a reverse proxy, the `Host` checked is the
one the proxy forwards: keep it the browser’s (Caddy and nginx can).

* **Parameters:**
  * **attachment_store** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)]) – Where `process_submission` put the screenshots.
  * **config** ([`HeedConfig`](_autosummary/heed.config.html.md#heed.config.HeedConfig) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Defaults for `signer` (`attachment_signing_key`,
    `attachment_url_ttl_seconds`) and `allowed_hosts`
    (`attachment_hosts`).
  * **signer** ([`AttachmentSigner`](_autosummary/heed.serving.html.md#heed.serving.AttachmentSigner) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Required unless `allow_unsigned`: report ids are not secret.
  * **allow_unsigned** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Serve any ref without a signature (a ref is then the
    capability). Only for stores whose every screenshot may be public.
  * **allowed_hosts** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Hostnames this route answers on: the dedicated attachment origin.
    Required (here or as `config.attachment_hosts`): `ANY_HOST` says any
    host is fine, which is only right when the route has no origin of its own.
  * **cross_origin** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin`, which an image
    embedded in a GitHub issue needs (GitHub’s camo proxy fetches it).
  * **cache_control** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Replaces the `Cache-Control` of a served image (default
    `private, no-store`), e.g. `public, max-age=300` if GitHub’s camo proxy
    should cache signed, cross-origin images. Defaults to
    `config.attachment_cache_control`.
  * **max_bytes** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Stored values larger than this are not served (a bare 404 and a
    warning). Defaults to `config.max_screenshot_bytes`. It does not stop a
    store from reading the value into memory; it keeps serving from relying on
    the ingest cap alone.
  * **ref_pattern** ([`Pattern`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/re.html#re.Pattern)) – Refs to serve (full match); the default is what heed writes.
* **Return type:**
  `APIRouter`

### heed.serving.screenshot_url_resolver(base_url, signer, , ref_pattern=re.compile('[0-9a-f]{32}\\\\.(?:png|jpg|webp)'))

A `GitHubIssuesSink(screenshot_url=...)` callable: the report’s first image
attachment as a (signed) URL under `base_url`, or None.

Pass `signer=None` only if the attachment route was built with `allow_unsigned`.
Refs the route would not serve (`ref_pattern`) get no URL.

# _autosummary/heed.sinks.base.html.md

# heed.sinks.base

The sink abstraction — where a report goes (strategy pattern).

A sink is the only thing that decides what becomes of a report. The ingest layer calls
`Sink.submit()`; richer sinks may also offer duplicate detection and
acknowledgement, and may list its public items for a board ([`heed.board`](_autosummary/heed.board.html.md#module-heed.board)). New
destinations are added by writing a sink, never by editing a dispatcher.

# _autosummary/heed.sinks.category.html.md

# heed.sinks.category

A sink that sends each category of report to its own sink.

One widget and one [`Report`](_autosummary/heed.base.html.md#heed.base.Report) cover a bug, a feature request and a
question; the sink decides what each becomes. [`CategorySink`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.category.html.md#heed.sinks.category.CategorySink) is that decision as
data: bugs to the tracker, feature requests somewhere else (a second repo, a Discussions
sink, a store), anything unlisted to `default`. It is itself a sink, so it nests under
[`sinks_by_origin()`](_autosummary/heed.routing.html.md#heed.routing.sinks_by_origin) and under moderation like any other.

```pycon
>>> from heed.sinks import StoreSink
>>> bugs, ideas = StoreSink({}), StoreSink({})
>>> sink = CategorySink({"feature": ideas}, default=bugs)
>>> sink.sink_for("feature") is ideas and sink.sink_for("bug") is bugs
True
```

### Classes

| [`CategorySink`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.category.html.md#heed.sinks.category.CategorySink)(sinks, \*, default)   | Route by `report.category`; unlisted categories go to `default`.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|

# _autosummary/heed.sinks.github.html.md

# heed.sinks.github

A sink that turns a report into a GitHub issue.

The issue-creating call is dependency-injected (`create_issue`) so the sink is
testable without network access and so the credential-brokering strategy (a GitHub App
minting short-lived installation tokens, or a server-side token) is pluggable. A
convenience factory builds a `create_issue` from a token via `ghapi` (lazy import,
the `heed[github]` extra).

Hard platform limit (see misc/docs/design.md): there is no GitHub API to attach an image
to an issue. Resolve a `screenshot_url` (committed-file / attachment-store URL) and
embed it in the body; base64 data-URIs do not render.

### Module Attributes

| [`DEFAULT_STATUS_LABELS`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.github.html.md#heed.sinks.github.DEFAULT_STATUS_LABELS)   | Issue labels a maintainer applies to move an item along; the board reads them back.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`MAX_BOARD_PAGES`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.github.html.md#heed.sinks.github.MAX_BOARD_PAGES)         | The most pages (of 100 issues) one board read will fetch.                             |
| [`DEFAULT_PUBLIC_LABEL`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.github.html.md#heed.sinks.github.DEFAULT_PUBLIC_LABEL)    | A maintainer adds this label to put an item on the public board.                      |

|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`neutralise_refs`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.github.html.md#heed.sinks.github.neutralise_refs)(text)                             | Defuse GitHub `@mention`, `#123`, issue-URL and SHA references.          |
| [`render_issue_body`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.github.html.md#heed.sinks.github.render_issue_body)(report, \*[, ...])              | Render a report as a GitHub-flavoured markdown issue body.               |

### Classes

|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`GitHubIssuesSink`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.github.html.md#heed.sinks.github.GitHubIssuesSink)(create_issue, \*[, ...])           | Route a report to a GitHub issue via an injected `create_issue` callable. |

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

What one category of report becomes as a GitHub issue.

`detail="light"` is the feature-request intake: the idea and who asked, without
the browser/console/network dump or a screenshot, which say nothing about a wish.

### heed.sinks.github.DEFAULT_PUBLIC_LABEL *= 'public'*

A maintainer adds this label to put an item on the public board. Opt-in, because the
title of an unmoderated report must not reach a public page by default.

### heed.sinks.github.DEFAULT_STATUS_LABELS *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Status](_autosummary/heed.base.html.md#heed.base.Status)]* *= {'duplicate': Status.duplicate, 'in progress': Status.started, 'planned': Status.planned, 'triaged': Status.triaged, 'wontfix': Status.declined}*

### *class* heed.sinks.github.GitHubIssuesSink(create_issue, , label_map=None, screenshot_url=None, treatments=None, list_issues=None, public_label='public', status_labels=None, allowed_report_labels=())

Bases: [`BaseSink`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.base.html.md#heed.sinks.base.BaseSink)

Route a report to a GitHub issue via an injected `create_issue` callable.

`treatments` says, per category, the labels, a title prefix and how much context
the issue carries (`label_map` is the older labels-only spelling and still wins
for labels). With `list_issues` it can also read its issues back as a board’s
[`PublicItem`](_autosummary/heed.board.html.md#heed.board.PublicItem) entries: only those carrying `public_label`, with
status from `status_labels` (or the issue’s closed state) and votes from the 👍
reactions.

#### public_items(, category=None)

The board’s items: issues labelled `public_label`, as `PublicItem`.

Empty without `list_issues`. Only title, category, status, link, votes and
dates leave the sink: never an issue body (which holds the reporter’s
environment and identity).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`PublicItem`](_autosummary/heed.board.html.md#heed.board.PublicItem)]

#### treatment(category)

The treatment applied to reports of `category`.

* **Return type:**
  [`CategoryTreatment`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.github.html.md#heed.sinks.github.CategoryTreatment)

### heed.sinks.github.MAX_BOARD_PAGES *= 10*

The most pages (of 100 issues) one board read will fetch.

### heed.sinks.github.github_sink_from_token(repo, token, \*\*kwargs)

Build a GitHubIssuesSink that creates issues in `repo` (‘owner/name’).

Requires the `heed[github]` extra. `token` is a server-side credential (a GitHub
App installation token or a PAT) — never shipped to the browser.

* **Return type:**
  [`GitHubIssuesSink`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.github.html.md#heed.sinks.github.GitHubIssuesSink)

### heed.sinks.github.neutralise_refs(text)

Defuse GitHub `@mention`, `#123`, issue-URL and SHA references.

A zero-width joiner after `@`/`#` stops GitHub notifying a user or cross-linking
an issue from the tracker’s account. Only the rendered issue is changed; the stored
report keeps the original text.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### heed.sinks.github.render_issue_body(report, , screenshot_url=None, light=False)

Render a report as a GitHub-flavoured markdown issue body.

`light` leaves out the environment, console and network (a feature request’s
intake; a screenshot the server kept is still linked): the idea, the page it came
from, and who asked.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

# _autosummary/heed.storage.html.md

# heed.storage

Storage helpers — dol-backed stores for reports and binary attachments.

Stores are plain `MutableMapping``s, so the rest of heed never depends on a specific
backend. Defaults are in-memory; pass a directory to persist to the filesystem, or
inject any ``dol` store (S3, Mongo, …).

### Module Attributes

| [`CLAIMS_ATTR`](_autosummary/heed.storage.html.md#heed.storage.CLAIMS_ATTR)   | the store its reports are claimed in while `heed.routing.release_held` sends them.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`make_attachment_store`](_autosummary/heed.storage.html.md#heed.storage.make_attachment_store)([rootdir, ...])      | A bytes store for attachments.                                            |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`make_holding_store`](_autosummary/heed.storage.html.md#heed.storage.make_holding_store)([rootdir, delete_func]) | A report store for held reports, with a dedicated claims store beside it. |
| [`make_report_store`](_autosummary/heed.storage.html.md#heed.storage.make_report_store)([rootdir, delete_func])  | A text store for report JSON.                                             |

### heed.storage.CLAIMS_ATTR *= 'heed_claims'*

the store its
reports are claimed in while `heed.routing.release_held` sends them.

* **Type:**
  Attribute a holding store made by `make_holding_store` carries

### heed.storage.make_attachment_store(rootdir=None, \*, delete_func=<built-in function remove>, follow_symlinks=False)

A bytes store for attachments. In-memory unless `rootdir` is given.

Deletion is permanent by default, for the reason given in `make_report_store`.
Reading a key whose file is a symlink leading outside `rootdir` raises
`KeyError`, so a misconfigured root cannot make the attachment route serve other
files; `follow_symlinks=True` opts out.

```pycon
>>> make_attachment_store()
{}
```

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)

### heed.storage.make_holding_store(rootdir=None, \*, delete_func=<built-in function remove>)

A report store for held reports, with a dedicated claims store beside it.

`release_held` and `recover_claimed` find the claims store on the holding store
(`heed_claims`), so a release lists only the reports being released right now,
not every held report (issue #21), and nothing listing holding (a moderation view,
`StoreSink.find_duplicates`) ever sees a claim. With `rootdir`, claims live in a
sibling directory, `<rootdir>.claims` (a subdirectory would show up in the
holding store’s recursive listing).

```pycon
>>> held = make_holding_store()
>>> held["r1"] = "{}"
>>> list(held), dict(held.heed_claims)
(['r1'], {})
```

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)

### heed.storage.make_report_store(rootdir=None, \*, delete_func=<built-in function remove>)

A text store for report JSON. In-memory unless `rootdir` is given.

Deleting a key removes the file for good (`os.remove`). dol’s own default moves it
to the OS trash, which would keep a copy of every deleted, claimed or released
report – and reports can carry personal data. Pass `delete_func` to opt back in.

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)


# _autosummary/heed.threads.html.md

# heed.threads

Comment threads: a persistent, public, append-mostly conversation per key.

A *thread* is the list of comments left under one thing (a review page, a video, a
document). Anyone who can reach the thread can read it and add to it; only a
moderator can delete. This module is the reusable core of that mechanism, independent
of what the thread is attached to (`heed.review` attaches it to a media page):

- [`Comment`](_autosummary/heed.threads.html.md#heed.threads.Comment) / [`CommentSubmission`](_autosummary/heed.threads.html.md#heed.threads.CommentSubmission) – the stored comment and what an
  untrusted client may send (a name, a body, optionally a position in a media item:
  `at_ms`, integer milliseconds, and `media`, the item’s name).
- [`add_comment()`](_autosummary/heed.threads.html.md#heed.threads.add_comment), [`list_comments()`](_autosummary/heed.threads.html.md#heed.threads.list_comments), [`delete_comment()`](_autosummary/heed.threads.html.md#heed.threads.delete_comment) – pure
  functions over ONE thread’s store, a `MutableMapping` of `{comment_id}.json`
  keys, so a `dict`, a folder or an S3 `dol` store all work.
- *Threads* are a callable `thread -> store`: [`memory_threads()`](_autosummary/heed.threads.html.md#heed.threads.memory_threads) (dicts) or
  [`folder_threads()`](_autosummary/heed.threads.html.md#heed.threads.folder_threads) (one folder per thread), so reading a thread never lists
  > any other thread.
- [`make_thread_router()`](_autosummary/heed.threads.html.md#heed.threads.make_thread_router) – `GET`/`POST` `/threads/{thread}` and
  `DELETE /threads/{thread}/{comment_id}`, hardened like heed’s ingest endpoint
  (per-IP and per-thread rate limits, per-thread cap, honeypot, body cap, strict
  validation).

Who may reach a thread is the host’s decision, passed in as `thread_exists`: an
unknown thread is a 404, so a thread keyed by an unguessable id is a capability.

```pycon
>>> store = {}
>>> sub = CommentSubmission(author="Noel", body="Nice cut", at_ms=1500)
>>> c = add_comment(store, "t1", sub)
>>> [(x.author, x.body, x.at_ms) for x in list_comments(store)]
[('Noel', 'Nice cut', 1500)]
>>> delete_comment(store, c.id)
True
>>> list_comments(store)
[]
```

### heed.threads.make_thread_router(threads=None, \*, thread_exists=<function valid_id>, is_moderator=<function no_moderator>, rate_limiter=None, rate_limit_per_minute=10, thread_rate_limiter=None, thread_rate_limit_per_hour=120, max_comments_per_thread=500, trusted_proxies=(), honeypot_field='website', on_comment=None, thread_gate=None)

The HTTP surface of comment threads (`threads`: thread id -> its store).

`GET /threads/{thread}` lists, `POST /threads/{thread}` adds (a JSON body:
`author`, `body`, optional `at_ms` and `media`),
`DELETE /threads/{thread}/{id}` deletes when `is_moderator(request)` and the
request carries the `X-Heed-Moderate` header. A thread for which
`thread_exists` is false answers 404 to everything, which is how a host makes
threads capabilities; `thread_gate(request, thread)` is called on every request
to an existing thread and raises `HTTPException` to refuse it (a password, say).
A filled `honeypot_field` is accepted silently and
stored nowhere. Behind a reverse proxy, set `trusted_proxies` or every visitor
shares the proxy’s rate-limit bucket.

```pycon
>>> from fastapi import FastAPI
>>> from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
>>> app = FastAPI(); app.include_router(make_thread_router())
>>> client = TestClient(app)
>>> client.post("/threads/t1", json={"author": "Thor", "body": "hi"}).status_code
201
>>> [c["body"] for c in client.get("/threads/t1").json()["comments"]]
['hi']
```

* **Return type:**
  `APIRouter`

### heed.threads.memory_threads()

Threads held in dicts, one per thread (tests, single-process demos).

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)]

### heed.threads.new_comment_id(\*, clock=<built-in function time>)

A comment id that sorts by creation time (ms, zero-padded) then at random.

```pycon
>>> a, b = new_comment_id(clock=lambda: 1.0), new_comment_id(clock=lambda: 2.0)
>>> a < b and len(a) == len(b)
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### heed.threads.no_moderator(request)

The default moderator check: nobody may delete over HTTP (use the CLI).

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### *async* heed.threads.read_capped(request, cap, , what='Comment')

The request body, refusing (413) anything over `cap` bytes while streaming.

* **Return type:**
  [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)

### heed.threads.token_moderator(token, , also=None)

A moderator check that needs a secret the owner types in, not a login.

On an origin shared with other apps, a session cookie is ambient authority: any
script running there while the owner is logged in can call the API *as* the owner.
A secret in a request header is not ambient (the review page keeps it in memory,
never in storage), so such a script can neither delete comments nor post badged as
the owner. `also` (e.g. [`email_moderator()`](_autosummary/heed.threads.html.md#heed.threads.email_moderator)) is required too, when given.

Use a random token (`secrets.token_urlsafe(24)`). This raises the bar, it is not a
wall: a hostile script on the same origin can still open the review page in a frame
and hook it before the owner types the token, or phish with its own prompt. A
dedicated origin for the review app is the real fix.

```pycon
>>> from types import SimpleNamespace as NS
>>> check = token_moderator("s3cret-token-value")
>>> check(NS(headers={"X-Heed-Moderator-Token": "s3cret-token-value"}))
True
>>> check(NS(headers={}))
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`Request`], [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)]

### heed.threads.valid_id(value)

Whether `value` is a safe thread or comment id.

```pycon
>>> valid_id("abc_DEF-1"), valid_id("../x"), valid_id("a.json")
(True, False, False)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)


# _autosummary/heed.widget.html.md

# heed.widget

Serve the embeddable widget, and state the contract it is built against.

The widget (TypeScript sources under `widget/` at the repository root) is built into
`heed/static/widget/` and shipped inside the Python package, so the backend that
receives reports can also serve the script that sends them: one host, no CDN, no npm
install for the embedding site.

Two things live here:

* [`make_widget_router()`](_autosummary/heed.widget.html.md#heed.widget.make_widget_router) serves the built files. Only the names listed in the
  build’s `manifest.json` are served (no path ever reaches the filesystem), with
  headers that let any site load them (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and
  `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin`, needed for Subresource Integrity and
  for pages with COEP) and long-lived caching for content-hashed names.
* [`widget_contract()`](_autosummary/heed.widget.html.md#heed.widget.widget_contract) is the single source of truth for what the widget sends:
  the form field names the ingest route reads and the limits `base.py` enforces.
  `widget/src/contract.gen.ts` is generated from it (`python -m heed.widget
  contract`) and a test fails when the two drift.

```pycon
>>> c = widget_contract()
>>> c["fields"]["title"], c["limits"]["title_chars"]
('title', 300)
```

### Functions

| [`load_widget_manifest`](_autosummary/heed.widget.html.md#heed.widget.load_widget_manifest)([asset_dir])   | The build's manifest: `{"version", "entries", "files": {name: {...}}}`.     |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`main`](_autosummary/heed.widget.html.md#heed.widget.main)([argv])                        | `python -m heed.widget contract`: print the generated TypeScript contract.  |
| [`make_widget_router`](_autosummary/heed.widget.html.md#heed.widget.make_widget_router)(\*[, asset_dir]) | A router serving the built widget at `GET /widget/{name}`.                  |
| [`render_contract_ts`](_autosummary/heed.widget.html.md#heed.widget.render_contract_ts)([contract])      | The TypeScript module `widget/src/contract.gen.ts` (generated, not edited). |
| [`widget_contract`](_autosummary/heed.widget.html.md#heed.widget.widget_contract)([config])           | What the widget sends and the limits it must respect (from heed's SSOT).    |

### heed.widget.load_widget_manifest(asset_dir=None)

The build’s manifest: `{"version", "entries", "files": {name: {...}}}`.

Returns an empty file list when the widget has not been built (a source checkout
that never ran `npm run build`), so the backend still starts.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### heed.widget.main(argv=None)

`python -m heed.widget contract`: print the generated TypeScript contract.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### heed.widget.make_widget_router(, asset_dir=None)

A router serving the built widget at `GET /widget/{name}`.

Include it beside [`heed.make_router()`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.make_router) (`make_app` does) so the widget is
served from the same host that receives its reports. `asset_dir` defaults to the
files shipped in the package; point it elsewhere to serve another build.

* **Return type:**
  `APIRouter`

### heed.widget.render_contract_ts(contract=None)

The TypeScript module `widget/src/contract.gen.ts` (generated, not edited).

```pycon
>>> render_contract_ts().splitlines()[0].startswith("// Generated")
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### heed.widget.widget_contract(config=None)

What the widget sends and the limits it must respect (from heed’s SSOT).

`config` supplies the server-configurable names (honeypot, bot token field) and
the screenshot cap; their defaults are what the widget assumes unless an embedder
overrides them.

```pycon
>>> widget_contract()["categories"]
['bug', 'feature', 'question', 'other']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

# ai-agents.html.md

<!-- generated by epythet -->

# For AI agents

`heed` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `heed-review`

Publish media (a video, audio takes, images) as a public review page with a persistent comment thread under it, send the link to someone who has no account (a writer, a client, a collaborator), and read their comments back so you can act on them. Use when the user asks for “a page where X can comment on the video”, “get feedback from <someone> on this cut”, “let them pick a voice in the comments”, “a review link”, “share this for comments”, “what did <someone> say about the video”, or when a published review page needs a new cut on the same link. Not for the owner’s private reading (that is annals-publish).

```bash
gh skill install i2mint/heed heed-review --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`heed/data/skills/heed-review`](https://github.com/i2mint/heed/tree/HEAD/heed/data/skills/heed-review) (bundled with the pip package).

The bundled skills are also on disk after `pip install heed`, under the package’s `data/skills/` directory; link them into an agent without network access with `skill link-skills <that directory>`.

## Instruction files

Files agents read before working in this repository.

- [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/i2mint/heed/tree/HEAD/CLAUDE.md): read by Claude Code

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://i2mint.github.io/heed/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`heed.md`](https://i2mint.github.io/heed/heed.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://i2mint.github.io/heed/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
